17.Content: Gentlemen, hold your horses. It's pointless to fight you. Once we're done here, anything you say to the Brotherhood will be without proof. Let's go.

18.Content: You wanna go after them?

19.Content: No, we should head back to the Brotherhood right away.

0.Content: What's going on? The Academy made their move?

1.Content: My medallion... Something is not right.

0.Content: Damn it! They're all gone. It's over!

1.Content: Wait, what happened? Who's gone?

2.Content: Those morons from the Academy! I told them not to rush the attack, but they didn't listen. Graveborns controlled by the traitor smashed them down…

3.Content: And there's more… The traitor is performing a magic rite that will transform the sorcerers from the Astral Academy into Graveborns.

4.Content: Shit! If they join traitor's forces as Graveborns… no one will stop him. Not even the Brotherhood.

5.Content: We don't have time to wait for backup. We have to act now.

6.Content: I know. Yen? Any ideas?

7.Content: It's risky, but… I could use the Arcane Portal. I think there's a way to cast a reverse spell to destroy the Graveborns. Possibly even break the traitor's spell. But I'm gonna need time…

8.Content: We will buy you time.

0.Content: Yennefer, did you figure it out?

1.Content: Yes, I'm ready, it's just that… I can't do it without destroying the portal. I just don't know enough about magic in this world. If I could spend some more time in the Astral Academy…

2.Content: It's alright, Yen. Just do it. We will find another portal.

3.Content: Yes, I guess we will. It just never goes as planned, hm? Hold tight. Let's get it started.

0.Content: …That's what happened. In the end the sorcerers of the Astral Academy avoided a disaster. But only thanks to… my two friends here.

1.Content: We are very grateful, Mr Geralt. Please accept our apologies. And thank you too, Ms Yennefer. Your courage and selflessness will be remembered by the Brotherhood.

2.Content: As I promised, I asked in the Brotherhood about the Arcane Portal. Mirael drew me a map with the probable locations. I believe it will be useful to you.

3.Content: Let me see… It's more than just a map! With this, we can predict when and where the next Arcane Portal will appear.

4.Content: Mr Geralt, the witcher, you have more than proven yourself with the Brotherhood. An expert like you is qualified to take any commission!

5.Content: If you need any help, you know where to find me.

6.Content: I told you, Fawkes, that I work alone.

7.Content: So… It looks like we have some time before the next portal appears.

8.Content: I know that smile, Geralt. What are you up to?

0.Content: According to this map I've bought with a fortune, Limestone Village should be just up ahead.

1.Content: We're surrounded by mountains, but the terrain is barely vegetated. Are you sure the magical herb you're looking for is really here?

2.Content: Of course! If it grew everywhere, you wouldn't call it "rare", would you?

3.Content: Yes, but it looks deserted here...

4.Content: Maybe it's just right over this mountain. Who knows? Why don't we focus on finding our way to Limestone Village?

0.Content: It's a huge rock, and it's blocked the road completely!

1.Content: I hear voices in the wind, coming and going. Looks like we have to cross these mountains to reach the village.

2.Content: I see why no merchants travel here to buy herbs...They wouldn't be able to get in at all!

3.Content: Calm down now. I smell gunpowder, and there seems to be an artillery battery up ahead. Perhaps we could blast our way through with cannons.

4.Content: Cannons...They can fetch a good price. If I could sell them to…

5.Content: Stop thinking about being a firearms dealer. We have more pressing matters at hand!

0.Content: Cannons can be dangerous. You'd do well to be careful when you handle them.

1.Content: These cannons are in mint condition! They would sell very well in the city.

2.Content: I see a lot of fallen rocks here. The artillery batteries were probably placed here long ago for clearing rocks.

3.Content: Clearing rocks with cannons sounds dangerous. But I guess it can't be helped, seeing how perilous the landscape is.

0.Content: Wow it just teleported us…Is this magic?

1.Content: No, I think we triggered some kind of device which teleported us here instantly. How amazing!

2.Content: This is the first time I'm seeing something like this...There are all manner of contraptions in these mountains not seen in the empire. If I could just modify and sell them, I would make a handsome profit!

3.Content: It is probably operated by a special mechanism, which is beyond our minds to fathom. I can sense it bears an ancient wisdom…

4.Content: You can study the thing later. Now let's keep moving! Who knows, Limestone Village might be close by.

0.Content: Didn't I say? We're at Limestone Village. But why does it look so deserted…

1.Content: I don't see a soul.

2.Content: Who are you?

3.Content: Hello! We're travelers coming here to find some herbs...Is this Limestone Village?

4.Content: Indeed. I am the village chief. But we haven't had any visitors for a long time...What are you doing here?

5.Content: Sir, my partner and I have heard of a rare herb that is found in these parts. That's why we've come here.

6.Content: (Although I hardly see any crops––it doesn't look like a place that can grow herbs.)

7.Content: Pardon my rudeness, gentlemen. I see you come with good intentions. But our village is now barren. You might have to seek your herb elsewhere.

8.Content: "Cross the mountains and look upon the fertile land of Limestone." That's what the map says. We've blasted a few rocks and hills, but there's still no fertile land in sight. Could we have gone the wrong way?

9.Content: The soil here, though dry, holds great energy. It shouldn't be this arid.

10.Content: Chief, we're not here to ask for anything…Since this is Limestone Village, my map tells me that we should be standing on fertile land. Would you mind telling us what happened here?

11.Content: Oh that's a long story. Indeed, Limestone Village used to be a lush paradise with all sorts of precious herbs growing in abundance. However, we have been without rainfall for years now, with frequent landslides making matters worse. The upstream of the river has been blocked by fallen rocks, so we've been struggling to get enough water to survive ourselves, let alone watering the crops.

12.Content: So... that means you did have herbs here, but they've all withered?

13.Content: Limestone Village relies on its surrounding river for irrigation. But there are only the old and sick, as well as children left in the village. We don't have anyone to blast the river mouth and channel the river water into our village. Can you think of any way we could do that?

14.Content: If there was a cannon, then we might use it to blow open the river mouth and direct the water in.

15.Content: If you could bring in the water, Limestone Village would be able to restore its former glory…I'd get you all the herbs you need if you could help us!

16.Content: Sounds like a decent deal. But what if you don't have the herbs we want?

17.Content: Let's just see if we can find a cannon or explosives first, and blast the river mouth with them. We can talk about the herbs later.

18.Content: Fantastic. Come with me, I'll take you to the river mouth... If my memory serves me right, there's a cannon there!

0.Content: That's weird...I remember there was a cannon here. But why…

1.Content: Looks like we need to go into the mountains again and see if we can move the cannon here.

0.Content: It's water from the river…We're saved! Hurray!

1.Content: Phew! That was a lot of work…

2.Content: So, as we were discussing about the herbs…

3.Content: Oh yes. When you were up in the mountains, I went to ask our most learned elder in the village. He mentioned a herb called "Fable's Heart".

4.Content: Legend has it that Fable's Hearts are herbs blessed by the gods and can heal those who are on the brink of death. But it's never been said that they could bring the dead back to life.

5.Content: That's not what I've heard. Could the rumor from the market be false? We may have just made a wasted trip then…

6.Content: Oh I'm not finished yet. Fable's Hearts may not be able to revive the dead, but their healing properties are not something to be trifled with. The most expensive medicines in the empire may only have a fraction of its efficacy. The noble folk used to send people here to look for the herbs…

7.Content: Let me do the maths. The most expensive medicines now…Oh yeah, the herbs would indeed be extremely valuable.

8.Content: We turned away people who were willing to buy Fable's Hearts at an exorbitant price. But since you've literally saved our village, we're happy to gift you all our Fable's Hearts. They may have died from the drought, but now that we have water, Fable's Hearts will be able to grow once again.

9.Content: Oh that is too generous.

10.Content: Wow that's not a bad pay-off. This trip is not wasted after all.

11.Content: I don't know about the growth cycle of Fable's Hearts…But I gather it wouldn't be short given how valuable it is.

12.Content: Our elder says Fable's Hearts take 50 years to grow. But it's worth the wait, since they are so rare and precious.

13.Content: Fifty years? It's just impossible to wait that long…

14.Content: I suppose all precious things must be earned with respect and reverence. Money is not always the ultimate measure.

15.Content: Oh well, there goes my investment!

0.Content: Fawkes, our destination is just up ahead. Damn these hilly roads. My legs are killing me!

1.Content: When I get to the village, the first thing I'll do is to find some villager's place and put my feet down for an afternoon.

2.Content: Stay vigilant and let's observe before entering the village. Three years ago, Old John had his throat cut in his dreams by the farmer that had taken him in.

3.Content: Well at least he didn't suffer. For a demon hunter, that's a pretty decent way to go.

4.Content: The fields here haven't been tended for at least a few months. I'm afraid something has happened to the villagers.

5.Content: Looks like our intelligence is outdated. I think our guns will be more reliable from now on.

6.Content: Watch out! There are some low-level Hypogeans roaming in front! They are blocking the way into the village.

7.Content: Let's get this over quickly and be careful not to startle other enemies.

0.Content: Damn it! And they said there are no traces of demons here?

1.Content: This place is too remote, and many "surprises" could've come to pass during our journey here. Let's be vigilant and keep going.

0.Content: Fawkes, there are signs of fighting everywhere. It looks like the village has been invaded by those low-level Hypogeans. The villagers have all been…

1.Content: Things may not be that straightforward. So far, we have yet to see a dead body of the villagers. I've never heard that Hypogeans bury their victims.

2.Content: Seems like there's more to it than meets the eye.

0.Content: There are some strange pieces of wood on the ground. They look like the fragments of a smashed statue. Let me try and piece them together.

1.Content: Some parts are missing, but we can tell it's a girl with butterfly wings.

2.Content: That's Tasi, the fairy of dreams. I reckon it's the Hypogean who's Tasi's nemesis that has brought nightmares to the village.

3.Content: So, the villagers were originally protected by Tasi, but her statue was later destroyed by the Hypogean. Hence the invasion by all these demons?

4.Content: That's a possibility.

0.Content: Did you see that farmhouse just now? Its doors were broken out from the inside.

1.Content: It's not just that one. I checked a few houses nearby, and there were more Hypogean claw marks inside than on the exterior walls.

2.Content: I also saw fragments of clothing in the houses. The garments didn't look like they had been shredded, but instead ripped open from the inside.

3.Content: I think we've probably already met the villagers.

0.Content: I think we should end our mission now. After all, we've done far beyond what is required for a survey mission.

1.Content: We may not have the whole truth, but it's the most reasonable speculation we can come up with.

2.Content: "The village lost the protection of Tasi, which led to invasions by Hypogeans. All the villagers are gone." That'll be our report.

3.Content: Can't wait to get a good night's sleep when I get back. But there's one more thing I need to do before that.

4.Content: I'll have to kick the daylights out of that fellow that gave us the wrong intelligence!

0.Content: Brrrrr... It's so cold here that I'm not motivated to do anything. I would have worn an extra layer if I knew we were coming to a place like this, then my hands and feet wouldn't be so freezing cold.

1.Content: Hahaha! Although cold wind and permafrost are the norms here, you don't need to worry because I have a piping-hot drink here. One sip is all you need to warm yourself from the inside out!

2.Content: You make some sense... But compared to that, we have crossed many mountains to come here, and the ice lotus you mentioned is in front of us, but I vaguely remember you saying that "finding the ice lotus is just the beginning"...

3.Content: That's right, that's right. You must know that I traveled through all of Hathor before I finally found out from a tavern boy that it is possible to get a lost brewing recipe if you follow the direction pointed out by these ice lotuses.

4.Content: Hah! I sure hope you didn't come across this news in a drunken slumber.

0.Content: Oh no! The path has been blocked by ice.
I can sense that this device is radiating fire magic all around us.
If we can activate the mechanism and connect the red runes on the ground, we should be able to transmit the active fire element in the red crystal to the blue crystal device on the other side...

1.Content: Hahaha, it looks like you've done quite a bit of research on magic.

2.Content: Only fire magic! You must know that I have a rather troublesome "opponent." She is one of the best at using fire magic. If only she is here right now.

0.Content: Raine, look over here. There are more mechanisms and more options now.

1.Content: Hmm... It looks correct, and the red inscription can also be illuminated by activating the elevator platform. However, to pass through here smoothly, we will need to find a suitable inscription route.

2.Content: Didn't we agree before coming that I'm here to provide the brawn, while you'll provide the brains?

3.Content: Hahaha, don't worry. I think you're smarter than Fawkes.

0.Content: The traps are more complicated here... But it also means we have more different options.

1.Content: Let's take it step by step. We followed the ice lotuses here. I believe we'll soon find the recipe I need.

0.Content: (Frowns deep in thought while staring at the mechanisms)

1.Content: Rather than wearing such a distressed expression, why don't you have a sip of a hot drink to refresh your mind?

2.Content: Rigby, you may be my employer, but you sure can keep your composure when our destination isn't far ahead.

3.Content: There's no need to be anxious since nobody else is here. Having a clear head is essential to solving the problem.

4.Content: Look, even if the base of this mechanism is somewhat different from the previous ones, maybe it just means that it can be controlled by two mechanisms.

5.Content: You make perfect sense. That's what it is! I understand now.

0.Content: This is the destination the ice lotuses were guiding us to. Although we endured some hardships along the way, the result isn't bad at all.

1.Content: I thought I was getting my hopes up. Who would have known that I really would find a new lost recipe here?

2.Content: The atmosphere is so rosy now. Old Rigby, shouldn't you invite me up for a drink?

3.Content: Hahaha! I believe you'll soon be able to try my new drink.

4.Content: When you're at the Noble Tavern next time, tell them you're my friend. I'll shout you to a drink or two.

0.Content: The Black Prison is up ahead. Is it really as horrifying as legend claims?

1.Content: More so, actually.

2.Content: I didn't expect it to be so remote. I thought it was located at the heart of Bantus.

3.Content: That's somewhat true. There's in fact more than one Black Prison. When Thoran first established the Court of Terror, he built prisons throughout the realm, for he would condemn dissidents to strengthen his grip on power.

4.Content: The most important one is located precisely at the heart of Bantus.

5.Content: The one we are heading to is one of the Black Prisons. As you can see, it's been abandoned.

6.Content: Otherwise we wouldn't be able to get in.

7.Content: To prevent prisoners from escaping, the Black Prisons were once rigged with all manner of traps. Most of the inmates who attempted to break out with me never managed to escape.

8.Content: Be careful. The place may be ruined, but there may yet be dangerous traps lying around.

9.Content: Walk through the vestibule, and we'll be in the Black Prison.

0.Content: This tombstone...

1.Content: Tortured souls are asleep under the tombstone. Only people who are in spiritual form can awaken them.

2.Content: The soul obelisk here was once an instrument for torturing souls. But we can harness its residual power now to transform ourselves temporarily into spiritual form.

3.Content: Their wits and will have been crushed, and they may attack anything in front of them.

4.Content: (Treznor lowers his head and looks at the tombstone in front) Whether you were a friend or foe, today I'm here to set you free.

0.Content: It's a bit ironic that an abandoned prison is actually still "operating".

1.Content: When the wardens left, they were reluctant to vanquish the "prisoners". So they let them continue to be tortured and eventually lose their sanity.

2.Content: Today, they will be set free.

3.Content: To us the Tainted, who will never deign to degrade ourselves, death is a relief.

4.Content: We may be able to escape the Black Prison, but never the curse of immortality.

5.Content: Let's head back to the Island of the Banished. At least the Tainted there can live in peace.

6.Content: Perhaps one day, the Tainted will get to be truly free too.

0.Content: Look at that candle in front of you. It was put there by the wardens to keep the souls from escaping. The candlelight will extinguish any soul that is within its range of light.
Maybe we can free these suffering souls with candlelight.
We're here.

1.Content: Of all the things I expected to find hidden around here, an island was not one of them.

2.Content: The Island of the Banished spends much of the year hidden in fog. To this place I have arrived as well—by accident too.

3.Content: Where is Nevanthi?

4.Content: She slumbers deep within the Island of the Banished, a place much cursed by the strife in these latter years. She has given so much of herself and her energy to protect the Tainted and, as a last resort, had to protect herself within a cage.

5.Content: This Elemental Strife must be dealt with at once! We should make a move.

6.Content: The Corruptors have already taken control of the island. Remain ever watchful!

0.Content: These Corruptors seem far more powerful than those of the desert!

1.Content: I fear a frontal assault could be too time-consuming.

2.Content: I can hold them off here for now, Baden. You're more familiar with the island's terrain. I suggest you look for another less obvious path inland.

3.Content: Alright then. I'll head back to the coast and sail in search of a better landing point. I might be able to circumvent the main Corruptor force.

4.Content: I'll make a path for you.

0.Content: There are far too many Corruptors here. We must find another way.
Nevanthi is just over there, but alas the bridge has been destroyed.

1.Content: We need to find the nearby Magic Circle.

0.Content: Wake up, Nevanthi.

1.Content: Baden?

0.Content: Oh no! They're after us.

1.Content: Corruptors are all over the island. There's nowhere to hide.

2.Content: We might be able to go around them on the northside. I've already readied an escape vessel by the coast.

3.Content: I'm already...

4.Content: Don't worry, I'll get you out of here.

5.Content: The elements are already in chaos... I've used too much power to suppress the corruption. Disaster is inevitable... You go find the other Elemental Guardians...

6.Content: I'll never abandon a friend.

7.Content: The Corruptors can sense the wood emblem on me... You'll have a better chance by yourself...

8.Content: It's not time to give up.

9.Content: Nevanthi, just hold on. Reinforcements are coming.

0.Content: Uh oh. This Corruptor is far more powerful!

1.Content: It's not the priority! Let's go, now!

2.Content: The island is shrouded in fog. It's remote and isolated. Reinforcements won't be able to find us easily. It'll be easier for one person to slip away...

3.Content: Go! Now! Before it's too late!

4.Content: Don't worry and let's just try our best to avoid him.

0.Content: It's coming!

1.Content: We must tread very carefully from here on. Know that any mistake could prove fatal.

0.Content: Nevanthi has set up a Magic Circle nearby. Light it up, and it should establish a bridge between the two cliffs.

1.Content: The Island of the Banished is filled with inhospitable mountainous terrain. The Magic Circles Nevanthi conjured is what the Tainted used to cross the chasms.

0.Content: If I recall correctly, there's another path nearby that leads to the shore. It's our only escape.
A dead-end...

1.Content: The strange changes wrought to the island have also done much to the local terrain.

2.Content: To fight is now our only option.

3.Content: We've just got to hold on until reinforcements arrive. We still have a chance.

0.Content: THANE!

1.Content: You're too badly wounded to fight.

2.Content: Our fight is unfinished!

0.Content: Look out!

1.Content: BADEN!

0.Content: Baden, my friend... I am powerless to restore you.

1.Content: But the Elemental Emblem can offer a metamorphosis instead!

2.Content: If you take it, you are giving up your hard-won peace to become a target of the Corruptors.

3.Content: Will you accept it?

4.Content: I have only dreamed of peace...

5.Content: It's my destiny to be chased by these shadows...

6.Content: However, I will never fight alone again!

0.Content: It's over, but there's still a tough journey ahead.

1.Content: It can't be any worse than what we've faced so far... We've all lost a lot, but even so, there are still things worth fighting for, even dying for.

2.Content: Then let us fight together again, Thane, like the old days.

3.Content: Just like the old days.

0.Content: Pippa, are you alright?

1.Content: I'm okay, Nemora. Where are we?

2.Content: I think we fell into those amazing paintings we saw just now.

3.Content: Oops! Is it because I accidentally touched one of them?

4.Content: It's okay. Let's find a way to get out of here.

5.Content: But the road ahead is blocked by tall and thick grass.

0.Content: Let me find my glasses... Ah, I just bumped into something!
There should be some use to this strange device.
*puts on glasses* I can see clearly now, but where's the tall grass? Looks all flat to me.

1.Content: Ah I think I got it. This arrow-like device can turn one type of terrain into another one that it's pointing at.

2.Content: You just triggered the device and turned the tall grass into a flat plain! We can move forward now. Pippa, you just figured out how this painting world works!

3.Content: Hehehe, have I?

0.Content: Looks like we've entered another painting.

1.Content: I remember seeing five paintings before we fell in.

2.Content: That means we may be able to get back after traveling through all five paintings. We've got this, Pippa. We've been through worse.

3.Content: I…I'll do my best.

0.Content: Who barged into my magical painting? Let me see… two furry little creatures?

1.Content: Hello sir! My name is Pippa, and this is my friend Nemora.

2.Content: Hey there, little ones. I'm a painter living here in seclusion.

3.Content: Mr. da Vinci, do you know how we can get out of here?

4.Content: Don't worry. Since you've made it here already, just keep going towards the end. Find the treasure chest, and you'll be able to get out.

5.Content: What, there's a treasure chest? Nemora, let's find this treasure chest! Who knows, there might be a giant acorn in there!

6.Content: Huh? Okay, alright.

7.Content: Wonderful! All the best with your adventures, little furry ones.

0.Content: Oh god. The road is blocked.
There's a road to the south that leads to the shore.
Hey Pippa, did Grandpa Ulmus say how hard this is gonna be?

1.Content: I'm sure it'll be a breeze! To remove the barrier up ahead, we just need to light up the rune mechanism.

0.Content: Huh? There are three mechanisms here. Are we supposed to light up all of them?

1.Content: Yep, but in what order? Hmmm… there are six clusters of mushrooms here…

2.Content: Oh, I think I got it! The number of mushroom clusters in each row indicates the order number of that row.

3.Content: Wow, you're so smart, Raku!

0.Content: Oh no, I can only see two rows of mushrooms here! The other one is blocked by those trees.

1.Content: How do we find out the number of mushroom clusters under the trees? Let me think of a spell…

2.Content: Leave it to me! I'm a math genius (if I use my fingers).

0.Content: Hey, some of the mushrooms are gone. And what's with that huge one over there?

1.Content: Oh dear, the small mushrooms have been absorbed by the big one.

2.Content: I heard that big mushrooms grow in a certain pattern. Maybe we can still figure out the number of small mushrooms based on the big ones?

3.Content: Can we really?

4.Content: Yes! Grandpa Arden told us about it before, but I can't remember the specifics. Pippa, can you recall anything?

5.Content: Let me think… right, mushrooms only grow this big if they're surrounded on all sides by mountains or other mushrooms. They absorb the smaller mushrooms around them. Any empty spots next to them used to have small mushrooms. Big mushrooms can only absorb small mushrooms next to them.

6.Content: You're amazing, Pippa! Now we can definitely figure out the number of small mushrooms and the correct order!

0.Content: Haha! We'll be able to get through the maze in no time!

1.Content: The finish line is just up ahead! But I have a feeling the test isn't over just yet…

0.Content: Wow! Look! It's statues of us!

1.Content: Wow! They must be our rewards from Grandpa Ulmus.

0.Content: The client offered us this bounty privately without going through the guild. I suppose he wants to keep it secret.

1.Content: He's gone from being a hawker to a wealthy merchant. I'd say he's no ordinary fella.

2.Content: Well, we're almost there. Let's go over what we know.

3.Content: Firstly, the client is a wealthy merchant in Oakenfell.

4.Content: Secondly, he was once a hawker, but many years ago he became rich all of a sudden after escaping from the Maulers.

5.Content: Thirdly, the merchant claims he is the victim of dark magic and that only a special potion from the Temple of the Seers can cure him of his illness.

6.Content: Our mission is to procure that special potion.

7.Content: It's said that voodoo originates from a bizarre and fanatic form of demon worship. I'm afraid our mission this time will be…

8.Content: Our client has paid us half the bounty in advance.

9.Content: ...very interesting.

10.Content: We are in Mauler territory. Stay alert.

11.Content: Shhh…Someone's here.

0.Content: I guess that's "desert hospitality" for you.

1.Content: I have a feeling we'll be receiving a lot more of this "hospitality" before reaching the Temple of the Seers.

0.Content: The Temple of the Seers looks more eerie and mystical than it sounds in the rumors.

1.Content: The guards here also less friendly than expected. They ignored our request and wouldn't pass it on to their elder.

2.Content: I think it's time to cause a scene.

3.Content: Alright, just don't overdo it.

0.Content: Halt.

1.Content: (Fawkes tells the elder the reason for their visit.)

2.Content: Well, I guess that ungrateful bastard finally got what was coming for him.

3.Content: Ungrateful?

4.Content: It was over 10 years ago. He got lost in the desert and passed out near the Temple of the Seers.

5.Content: We kept him outside the temple and tended to his wounds, but little did we expect that he would sneak in and steal a totem while we were distracted by an enemy raid.

6.Content: I guess that explains his wealth.

7.Content: A non-believer can't do much with a totem. At most, they might be able to perform some crude magic. But the more they use it, the more the power of voodoo will eat away at them.

8.Content: I suppose he had it coming then. But since we're here on his commission, we must bring back the potion.

9.Content: It is ready. And mind you, while it can cure him, he will also lose all the voodoo magic he has cast.

10.Content: It's his choice. But before you leave with the potion, you must pay for your intrusion of the Temple of the Seers.

0.Content: The elder just gave us the potion without much fuss. I guess the priests at the temple are friendlier than the rumors had us believe.

1.Content: Maybe the price of this potion is greater than mere gold. But that's got nothing to do with us. Our job's just to bring the potion back.

0.Content: How many months has it been since I started hunting this shapeshifting Hypogean? The darned thing is as slippery as they come, I'll give it that.

1.Content: Not to mention the way it's capable of summoning other Hypogeans to help whenever I come close. Then once again it slips through my fingers... and not for want of bruises.

2.Content: But I'd say it's a fair bet the shapeshifting Hypogean is hiding in that village just over yonder.

0.Content: Hey buddy, you awake? The name's Raine, I'm from the Bounty Hunters Guild. Notice any suspicious folk going in and out of the village lately?

1.Content: Suspicious folk? Like you? I've been watching over Stillwater, I haven't seen anybody suspicious but you.

2.Content: Idiot. If a Hypogean spat in your face you'd probably think it was rain. Where's your village chief? Take me to him.

3.Content: Idiot?! How about I throw you into the dungeon, then we'll see who's the idiot!

0.Content: Gah... What a perfect chance to teach this good-for-nothing a lesson he'll never forget. But the Guild's been on me about "collateral damage" and I'm not looking to get kicked out...

1.Content: Let me have a crack at him.

2.Content: Woah, where'd you pop out from? Hold on. I know you! Aren't you that ranger who hangs around the Land of the Exiles and chases the Quicksand Claws? You were following me! Out with it. What do you want?

3.Content: Easy there. It's nothing complicated. I picked up on the by and by you might know something about one "Savage Frank". And he just so happens to be the last one on my hit list.

4.Content: I know you've got your hands full hunting a bad customer, and that's fine with me. In fact, seeing as I don't gotta follow your Guild's silly rules, we could take it down a lot faster working together.

5.Content: So what do you say? Care for a little impromptu teamwork? I help you, and then once we're done you help me track down Frank?

6.Content: Huh! I guess that explains things... I'd appreciate finishing the contract as soon as possible—but let's get one thing clear, OK? The reward for this bounty's all mine.

7.Content: Come on now, at least give me a little something for my ammo expenses!

0.Content: Time to wake up!

1.Content: Huh? Who-who are you? Why the heck did ya give me a bump on the noggin?

2.Content: Hold your horses. We're the good guys. I really need you to take us to see your village chief.

0.Content: So you're the chief of this here village, I take it? I'm a bounty hunter. And this here is my assistant.

1.Content: I think you meant to say "partner"...

2.Content: Thank Dura you're here! Last week was a shocker—we've had a villager go missing almost daily. I've implemented a night curfew and tripled patrols, but nothing's working.

3.Content: We're on the hunt for a shapeshifting Hypogean. And I have good reason to suspect it may be hiding out somewhere in this village.

4.Content: What did you say? A Hypogean?! In our village?

5.Content: This particular Hypogean can change shape into pretty much anything it wants to. It's difficult for the average person to tell them apart from the original.

6.Content: Dura preserve us! Did I mention our village's bridge has also been damaged? I've tried to keep the whole thing under wraps and preserve the peace. But, bounty hunters, I beg of you to please help! Do everything you can to get rid of this Hypogean!

7.Content: I suppose we should start by questioning the locals.

0.Content: Hey, excuse me? You look like a carpenter. Are you?

1.Content: I look like a carpenter, do I? And who are you? Never seen you before. Folk 'round here would know I'm the village carpenter.

2.Content: All the carpenters I know back home are so busy they hardly get time to sit down for a proper lunch. How's business? Not too great from the looks of it?

3.Content: What am I supposed to do? My Annalisa's gone missing. Can't do anything to the wood without her.

4.Content: Annalisa?

5.Content: My ax. I tell you, with Annalisa here, I could turn the ugliest tree in the forest into a beautiful wooden sculpture of our sacred Dura.

6.Content: I take it you must be quite concerned about losing "Annalisa" then... So do you mind showing us where it was you lost her?

7.Content: The chief sent you here, huh? Very well. I had the misfortune of running into a Hypogean a couple of days ago while cutting wood up north.

8.Content: Did you say "Hypogean"?

9.Content: Truth is, I ain't never seen a Hypogean before. But with the awful "thing" I saw it's a fair bet I was looking at one—and it was changing shape.

10.Content: It must be the shapeshifting Hypogean. It can change into any shape it wants—or any person for that matter.

0.Content: Hold on—are you going hunting for that thing?

1.Content: Don't worry, buddy. We're more than capable of handling it.

2.Content: I hope so! I thought I was a goner! I ran all the way back. Ran so hard Annalisa fell off my belt and I didn't even notice!

3.Content: Do you... think you could go looking for her around the road north? Maybe you can bring my Annalisa back. I haven't dared. And the village bridge is broken. I'll need her to fix it.

4.Content: We will be sure to return it to you if we see it.

0.Content: This is your lucky day! Villagers, travelers, come one, come all! You do not want to miss out on the finest fruits and vegetables of the season, ripe and ready!

1.Content: Another day of ripening and I think most of these fruits are going into the bin.

2.Content: Well, this is just great, isn't it? I finally get two customers, but instead of buying my fruit, they just want to come and make fun of me.

3.Content: You think it was my choice to keep it on hand? Should've sold it all last week. But now everyone's running scared because of these darned disappearances. Plus we got the night curfew and that anonymous letter.

4.Content: Can't get any buyers if everyone's scared, can I?

5.Content: Just give it away before they rot, buddy.

6.Content: ... Great idea, "buddy." I'll just give away my hard-earned produce? Then no one's gonna buy from me ever again! They'll just wait 'til I give it away next time. Then I'll starve because I don't have any fields of my own.

7.Content: Changing the subject, you must have been around town buying from farmers quite a bit, eh? Seen any other newcomers? Or any villagers doing anything suspicious?

8.Content: Bounty hunter from the Guild, are you? And a ranger, from the looks of it? Come to think of it, there have been a few weird things going on in the village lately...

9.Content: What things?

10.Content: Alright then. You do me a solid and then I'll do you a solid—and tell you what I know.

11.Content: Excuse me? We're investigating on behalf of your own village chief.

12.Content: So what? I'm a businessman doing business. Help me pick the sapphire fruit off that tree opposite, and then I'll tell you.

13.Content: Ask a merchant for a toe, and the price'll be a foot.

0.Content: Here's your sapphire fruit.

1.Content: ...I was expecting more for all that picking. You weren't eating them, were you? Your lips are blue!

2.Content: Hey, I shot the fruit down and some of it happened to fall in my mouth. Blame physics, not me. We got your darned produce. Now tell us what you know!

3.Content: ...Alright. It's about that broken bridge on the north side of the village... So the village chief told everyone it was an accident, right? But I saw the village chief and a few guards heading to the bridge the night before it broke when I was moving my goods. It was really late.

4.Content: Are you trying to tell us that you think that the village chief destroyed his own village's bridge?

5.Content: I ain't saying nothin'! Draw your own conclusions.

6.Content: Eh. This is easily solved. Let's just go back and ask the chief what happened.

7.Content: Wait... I'd rather play our cards close to the chest. What if there is something going on between this village chief and the Hypogean? Asking about the bridge will reveal our hand. Let's inspect the bridge first.

0.Content: Just as I thought... These markings are unmistakable. It was someone using a tool that damaged this bridge.

1.Content: How about we grab a guard and "persuade" him to tell us the truth—did the village chief order the bridge to be destroyed?

2.Content: No. Just stop involving normal people. This bridge connects to the nearest road heading north of the village. If this is the route the Carpenter took back home when he fled, he must have come back over the bridge.

3.Content: And he's got a pretty good ax, it sounded like. It's the perfect tool to take out a bridge...

4.Content: I'd like to look around the area opposite. And then let's go back and see what the village chief has to say about all this.

0.Content: Village chief! We wanted to cross over to the other side of the lake, but couldn't because the bridge has been destroyed.

1.Content: Indeed. The loss of that bridge has sadly cut village off from the other side and whatever lies beyond. It's a dangerous place. So for my part I've been happy enough to forbid our villagers from travelling there.

2.Content: How do you think the bridge got destroyed?

3.Content: ...One morning, a few days ago, some villagers reported to me that they had discovered the bridge was damaged. I took some folk to investigate and we found an entire section had been ripped out—almost as if ripped apart in the jaws of some terrifying monster.

4.Content: And had you noticed anything unusual in the village up until that point?

5.Content: Up until then? No... not at all. Which is good—our village is a nice and peaceful place.

7.Content: Speaking of which, we still need to investigate whatever is going on over on the other side of the bridge. So is there another way over?

8.Content: There is. There's a longer way around on the west side of the village. But I don't think it's particularly safe. That's where a lot of folks have gone missing. But if you need to go that way, I'm happy to authorize it on behalf of the village.

9.Content: But I can't spare anyone to go with you! The villagers are starting to get really unhappy over the situation. I need all hands on deck to maintain order—for their own safety.

10.Content: We'll be just fine on our own, thank you. But a word of advice, chief... Please don't do anything heavy-handed before we get back.

11.Content: I've already sent a letter to the Guild asking them to send some more hunters.

0.Content: When did you find time to send a letter to the Guild?

1.Content: I didn't... I'm pulling a fast one on the chief. I don't want him getting too comfortable in our absence if there really is something wrong with him.

2.Content: ...Then we can't take too much time. If no one shows up after a while, he's going to be on to you.

0.Content: Alright. It's just another one of those situations—you can play it smart or play it dumb.

1.Content: ...What are you talking about?

2.Content: Go on a few more adventures and you'll understand.

3.Content: Hah! Would you take a look at all the hay and powder kegs? Seems a shame not to put it to good use...

0.Content: Careful... Hypogeans have the cabin surrounded.

1.Content: I'm starting to think I can't trust these Hypogeans! He said it'd be a one-on-one duel!

2.Content: Are these twisted things Hypogeans too?

3.Content: Lower-level Hypogeans, I think, unsuspecting victims drawn to this place. But don't get careless... I don't know how many reports I'm gonna have to write if you get yourself killed on my watch.

4.Content: Hah! I'm more interested in seeing what happens when I blast them to smithereens.

0.Content: Wait... Do you see that? There's something in the crop field.

1.Content: Stay back! You don't want to be anywhere you can't see the ground easily.

2.Content: I say, is that an ax? Maybe it's the same one last owned by that sad Carpenter?

3.Content: It's a pretty fine specimen, I must say. Look at the delicate wooden filigree work on the handle... I think this must be his "Annalisa."

4.Content: So who lives in that cabin? And how did the Carpenter's ax end up in the middle of a crop field?

0.Content: Who's in there!? Come out!

1.Content: Don't shoot! I'm just a farmer!

2.Content: Just a farmer? I don't think there are any farmers still breathing around here. Hypogeans are coming out of the woodwork. Care to explain how you're still alive?

3.Content: I am a farmer! I live around here!

4.Content: Live around here? You mean in the cabin next to the crop field?

5.Content: Yes! I found the Carpenter's ax a couple of nights ago when he was running past my field. I had intended to return it, but on the way our chief stopped me and forced me to use this ax to destroy the bridge.

6.Content: And then I had to make my own way back once the bridge was down. And I saw all these monsters in my house! So I hid in the wheat field all night. That's how the ax ended up here.

7.Content: ...It's a good thing to this house has been in my family for generations. It's got a secret basement only I know about. Thanks to that I'm still alive. But I'm not sure how much longer I would have lasted! Thank Dura you're here!

8.Content: Are you also getting strong vibes that there's something wrong with the village chief?

9.Content: Mm. And considering the chief has the whole place under his thumb, it's pretty far from ideal. Things are gonna get really bloody if he's entered into some kind of deal with the Hypogean. We'd better go back at once.

10.Content: I know a shortcut you can use to get back to the village real fast—and it goes through the backyard of the village chief's own house!

0.Content: Who in their right mind would leave these things all over the place?

1.Content: Good. You're starting to understand why I'm annoyed all the time.

0.Content: You... wretched Hypogean! Don't think I'm afraid of you! Guards! Get off your wretched bums and save me!

1.Content: Humph. I think our sudden return took the chief by surprise!

2.Content: Who's that? Bounty hunters? What are you doing here?

3.Content: Don't move a muscle! Just tell us what you know about that night the bridge was destroyed. What did you do?

4.Content: Hold on... are you packing your bags? What, are you intending to make a run for it?

5.Content: Ah... yes, well... bounty hunters... this is all just one big misunderstanding. I wasn't about to leave the village. I've just been thinking about taking a little trip...

6.Content: (Loads gun)

7.Content: ...Alright then. I'll come clean with you. On the night it was destroyed, we'd received reports earlier of suspicious activity north of the village. I thought it was bandits! So I took some guards to the bridge to intercept them.

8.Content: It was only after we got to the bridge that I saw what was really happening on the other side. There were dead bodies everywhere. We weren't up against bandits, but something much worse—monsters! I don't think humans could have wrought that much destruction.

9.Content: I didn't have the guts to go further and see what we were up against. We retreated over the bridge to take a better look in the light of the morning. And that's when we discovered that the bridge had been mysteriously destroyed!

10.Content: I didn't want to let the villagers know my incompetence... and what would people think if they knew our bridge had been destroyed? Not to mention the bodies. So I ordered everyone to keep quiet. Believe me, I have no idea what's going on with this Hypogean. I would never betray my village to those evil monsters! And if you don't believe me, just ask any of my guards. They saw the whole thing.

11.Content: Yeah, yeah, I saw everything that night. People running for their lives to get back over the bridge... but none of 'em made it. Something dragged 'em away. I have no idea what. We wanted to get their bodies the next day, but then they were gone!

12.Content: Then how do you explain all of the Hypogeans just hanging out in your backyard?

13.Content: I truly don't know... but I can tell you that my family has kept a very valuable heirloom hidden around our house for many years—an enormous Energy Crystal our ancestors won in the Hypogean War long ago...

14.Content: Our family records say it was won by the empire with great difficulty from the Hypogeans' hands.

15.Content: An Energy Crystal? My goodness. No wonder the place is infested with Hypogeans! That Hypogean must be trying to reactivate the Crystal so they can use it again!

16.Content: No one from the village has been in my backyard for generations... How did you know?

17.Content: It was that farmer that told us. Hey... where's the farmer gone? I thought he came back with us.

18.Content: The farmer? Darn it! We've been had! The farmer was the shapeshifting Hypogean all along!

19.Content: He must have followed us into the chief's backyard! Curses. Should have picked up on it before—I was distracted by all those Hypogeans he summoned along the way. Now he's made off with the Hypogean Crystal while we weren't looking...

20.Content: Are you going to take on that Hypogean? I can help. My ancestors inscribed some magical runes on the Crystal a long time ago. It means you can use a scroll to open up a portal to an area near wherever the crystal is currently.

0.Content: Man was NOT meant to move that way. I think I'm going to be sick...

1.Content: Save your complaints for someone who cares! Time's a-wasting, we've got to stop that Hypogean ritual right now!

2.Content: Haha! Well done! I really didn't expect you to show up on such short notice. Regardless, you're too late. I've already released the energies within the Crystal. That means I will soon have access to a never-ending supply of Hypogean soldiers with which to shake the foundations of your poor little village!

3.Content: I really have to thank you for making all of this possible! Even my powers could not have broken through the enchantment on the Crystal. I needed a human being to give me access—which you provided by leading me straight to the Crystal in the chief's backyard.

4.Content: Darn it! You played us pretty well. But let's see how many shells you can take to the face!

5.Content: That should just about do it. Over there! (Raine points to the powder kegs by the side of the crop field).

6.Content: Humph! Hypogean bodies don't writhe nearly as much as I expected.

0.Content: Curses! How did he summon so many Hypogeans here already?

1.Content: We've got a Hypogean party in the village chief's backyard!

0.Content: What's going on? What have you done? You've destroyed the blue fruit trees. We needed them to make blue fruit pies for the village chief!

1.Content: Guards! These intruders are destroying the village chief's property! Arrest them!

0.Content: What idiot put powder kegs by the field! It was that conniving farmer! He managed one last laugh after I killed him...

1.Content: I could have led a great Hypogean crusade into your world...

2.Content: You can take that crusade and shove it!

0.Content: I must say, that was a very satisfying victory. And I think we've eliminated that Hypogean too.

1.Content: Don't worry about our bargain. I haven't forgotten. I'll get right onto finding your nemesis after I get back.

2.Content: Great to hear it! I must say, Guild membership does come with a few perks—notwithstanding my assistant role this time.

0.Content: Thank you for returning Annalisa! And I've also managed to fix the bridge in these past two days. Now anyone can come and go as they please.

1.Content: Be sure not to lose it next time, OK? Especially since you've named it.

0.Content: I'll be sure to make plenty of crutches and stretchers for our injured. Can't do much without Annalisa, but we'll manage.
Thank you, bounty hunters. But in the short time you've been away looking for that Hypogean, our village has been surrounded by its allies!

1.Content: A combination of guardsmen and village militia barely held them off—thank Dura—but we've taken enormous losses.

0.Content: Well, here we are. Don't go looking for trouble. You plan on paying for the powder kegs and hay we just lit up?
Well... that's vague.

1.Content: It's the same strange letter we heard about.

2.Content: It seems to be inviting us to meet the Hypogean by a crop field?

3.Content: Who knows? Never trust a Hypogean.

4.Content: Well, I can tell you one thing the Hypogean doesn't know—that we're packing four muskets.

0.Content: I didn't notice this cabin at first. But it smells of rotting plants. Do you think it could be...?

1.Content: All the flowers are in full bloom. But when I last came here they were all weathering on the vine.

2.Content: What? You've been here before?

3.Content: Oh sure. I stopped for a night here. I also noticed some shadowy figures moving outside in the dead of night, but one blast from my musket sent 'em packing.

4.Content: And there are also marks to indicate someone came running this way from the village. That's how I found the village—by following the track they left.

5.Content: You might have run into some Hypogeans yourself—or maybe it was the real farmer who had lured the Hypogeans away.

6.Content: But it looks like the "real" farmer didn't die here. Maybe he even managed to outrun the Hypogeans and is still alive.

0.Content: Guards, the time has come to defend our peaceful Stillwater! Now take up your weapons and do battle against the Hypogeans!

1.Content: ...That won't be necessary. The Hypogean may have released the Crystal's energy, but we still got 'em.

2.Content: Really? Thank you so much, brave bounty hunters!

3.Content: And one other thing... I didn't do my job properly here. I didn't serve my community as I should have. So I've decided to hold a new election for village chief.

4.Content: And who are the candidates?

5.Content: I saw that farmer who lives alone outside the village that night when we were sorely pressed by the Hypogeans. He ran around until he got their attention, and then took off in the other direction! He's a real hero in my eyes—he probably saved quite a few folks.

6.Content: But we haven't seen him since.

7.Content: Even if there is only a faint chance that he is still alive, we'll keep searching. The farmer did all he could to protect our peaceful village, and for that we must call him a true hero.

8.Content: I wish you the best of luck in your search.

0.Content: Remember, the Carpenter said that his ax must have been lost somewhere nearby.

1.Content: Yes. We can have a look around that farmstead.

0.Content: Alright, let's see, let's see... Which way could it be?

1.Content: Pardon me, Mr. Reindeer? Do you know the way to the Midwinter Wonderland?

2.Content: Hey there, my tiny, fuzzy-eared friend! Are you looking for the Midwinter Wonderland, too?

3.Content: My name's Satrana, thank you very much. And who are you calling tiny? We're practically the same height!

4.Content: Do you know the way to the Midwinter Wonderland?

5.Content: Oh, uh... O-Of course I do! And since you're in such a hurry to get there, allow me to show you the way!

6.Content: Great, thanks!

7.Content: If you want to enter the Midwinter Wonderland, you'll need to take a ride on this reindeer-drawn sledge and collect 3 invitations to reach the park's gate.

8.Content: When you're ready to depart, just ring this bell and the reindeer will spring into action.

0.Content: But something's blocking the sledge's path!

1.Content: Heheheh... Nothing in life comes easy, does it? You'll need to find a way to get the sledge safely to its next stop.

0.Content: Great, we've reached the first stop!

1.Content: You should be able to get your first invitation from that house up there.

0.Content: I got my first invitation! It says they'll be waiting for me in the park... We have to keep going!

1.Content: Hey, I'm just here to help you out. Besides, who cares about some stupid amusement park, anyways...

0.Content: Wow... We finally made it to the Midwinter Wonderland! Let's go win some prizes, Audrae!

1.Content: Prizes? What do I look like, a little kid?

2.Content: You've been looking for this place all along, right Audrae? I could tell from our little adventure together... You were so kind and determined to help, just like any other good child.

3.Content: I'm sure you can get into the park, too!

4.Content: You think so? Well then, I guess we could take a look around...

0.Content: Just look at all the lights and merry-go-rounds... It's so beautiful!

1.Content: Riding on a merry-go-round is a lot more fun than staring at it, don't you think?

2.Content: What? You mean... We can ride on it?

0.Content: Wow, what a pretty dress!

1.Content: You like it? I wanted to wear my best dress here, so I could be the prettiest princess in the park!

3.Content: Wait, your clothes look very nice, too! What material is that? And how did you get the wings to stay on so well?

0.Content: Ah, this could be a problem... And after all the trouble I went through to get into the Midwinter Wonderlands! I just wanted to sell some souvenirs... I wasn't expecting Princess Peggy to be here, too!

1.Content: Shhh! Quiet down, you two. Now then, could I interest you in some limited-edition Midwinter Wonderland badges? I've also got some scarves and mittens here...

0.Content: Heeheehee! You won't get anywhere with me, now hurry up or the grand prize will be as good as mine!
Pfffft! You're nothing special, after all. Quit wasting time, or you'll miss out on the grand prize!
Hey! How could you leave me behind like that! We could've easily taken those two out and claimed the grand prize for ourselves!

1.Content: Look who's talking! You threw off my entire strategy by getting in the way!

2.Content: It's all your fault!

3.Content: No, it's all your fault! Your fault!

0.Content: Here, it should start working again if I transfer some energy into it.
Wow, it worked! Come on, Stitchy, let's go for a ride on the merry-go-round!

1.Content: Great idea! I shall draft a blueprint of its design right away. The children will definitely buy tickets for its outside counterpart!

2.Content: This park is perfect for a princess like me! Wait... Is that Rowan?! Get back here, you dirty rat!

3.Content: This is what I've been waiting for!

4.Content: I want to ride, too!

0.Content: Elijah! Where are you, Elijah? Oh, pardon me, but have you seen a little boy around here?

1.Content: No, I haven't seen anyone on this road at all...

2.Content: Well, I'm looking for my little brother. He's not very tall... In fact, he's about your height!

3.Content: You really didn't need to add that last part...

4.Content: Do you think you could help me look for him? I think he might have gotten lost out in the wilds...

5.Content: I suppose... I was just on my way to scout out the road from the wilds to Harmony City, anyways.

0.Content: Now I can see why nobody takes a shortcut here: the weather is terrible, and the place is overrun by wild animals. I should try to stick to the main roads from now on...
He's nowhere near as tall as me... Come on, kiddo. Your sister's worried sick, now let's go find her.

1.Content: I know, I know! And don't call me "kiddo"!

0.Content: Elijah! Oh, thank goodness you're okay! I could never repay you for this, but please take this candle. It's a specialty from our hometown.
Let me think, let me think...

1.Content: Um, pardon me, but you're blocking the entrance to the silk shop...

2.Content: Oh, my apologies! These two young ladies have put me in quite the bind... Say, you look like a fairly capable merchant! Might I ask for your assistance?

3.Content: Our butler friend wishes to buy a gift for his master's wife, and this bolt of silk is the perfect choice! Just have a tailor fashion it into a dress for her, and I'm certain the lady will be the life of any party!

4.Content: I'm an expert when it comes to picking out quality goods, and silk does sound like a good idea. Can you show me which of your prints is the most popular? I'd like to take some home with me, as well.

5.Content: No, no, no! Don't listen to her! You say it's nearly the lady's birthday, yes? It'll take days for even the best tailor to turn that silk into a suitable dress! Why not buy her a sachet, instead? These are elegant, high-quality, and can be used at any time!

6.Content: A sachet would be lovely... What kind of scents do you carry? Are your prices open for negotiation?

7.Content: I implore you to choose wisely, good sir. After all, how could a measly sachet capture the beauty and dignity of your master's beloved wife? Only a dress of the finest silk will make her shine above the rest!

8.Content: And just how is she supposed to "shine" in a half-finished dress? Your silk is completely out of the question!

9.Content: Enough, you two! I can't hear myself think, either!

10.Content: If you have any bright ideas, good sir, now would be the time to speak!

0.Content: Well, silk really is a fine choice for a gift... If you're really tight on time, why not make a nice shawl out of it instead of a dress?

1.Content: That sounds like a wonderful idea! I'm certain milady would love that!

2.Content: Thank you for your support! Here is a small gift for your troubles.

3.Content: Thanks, though I also would've accepted a discount on your silk!

0.Content: Well, a sachet would save everyone a lot of stress, and she can even carry her favorite scent wherever she goes. I'm sure that would make her stand out at any banquet, too.

1.Content: That sounds like a wonderful idea! I'm certain milady would love that!

2.Content: Thank you for your support! Here is a small gift for your troubles.

3.Content: Thanks, though I also would've accepted a discount on your sachets!

0.Content: Hello, I'd like to purchase some Sage Blueberries. How was the harvest this year?

1.Content: The harvest was fine, but a thief has been making a lot of trouble for us lately. Help us capture that hoodlum, and I'll cut you a good deal on my blueberries!

2.Content: It's a deal!

0.Content: No, please! Have mercy!

1.Content: No can do. You've caused enough problems around here, and that farmer has every right to teach you a lesson.

2.Content: I'm sorry! Please, just let me go, and I swear I'll never steal another fruit for the rest of my life!

3.Content: Ugh... Out! Don't ever show your face!

4.Content: Oh, I can't thank you enough! Here, these are the blueberries I was going to steal. Take them!

5.Content: Huh? Okay...

0.Content: I'm sorry, the thief got away... But not before I managed to knock some sense into him. I don't think he'll be coming back anytime soon.

1.Content: I suppose that works, too. Much obliged, friend.

0.Content: Pardon me, but are you traveling through the mountains? I'm afraid my grandfather is trapped somewhere up there... Could you please help me look for him?

1.Content: Sure, I was just on my way to do some business in the mountains, as well. Do you have any clues as to where he might be?

2.Content: Well, my grandfather is a zoologist. Before he went missing, he said he was looking for a certain animal, one that only lives on snow-covered mountains. That's why I came here, but... I still haven't found him.

3.Content: An animal that only lives on snow-covered mountains, huh? I'll do my best...

4.Content: Thank you so much! And don't worry, money isn't a problem. Even if you don't find my grandfather, I'll still pay you for your troubles.

0.Content: Hey, gramps! Wake up!

1.Content: Urgh... Oh, dear...

2.Content: You're hurt... What happened to you? Here, let me help you up...

3.Content: Ah! The Burnybara!

4.Content: What?

5.Content: A unique organism that only lives in the vicinity of hot springs on snow-covered mountains... For the longest time, we believed that they could eat fire, but it turns out they actually BREATHE fire! Their extraordinary digestive system allows them to subsist on sulfuric crystals...

6.Content: ...Is this really the time for a biology lesson? Why don't you start by explaining what happened to you, instead?

7.Content: I remember now... It was that damned poacher! He was following me the entire time, and once I tracked down a Burnybara... He knocked me out and ran off with it! You have to help me rescue it! That Burnybara is a rare specimen, and we can't let some poacher have his way with it!

8.Content: My job was to rescue you, not this "Burnybara"... Don't you know how worried your granddaughter is right now?

9.Content: But we can't leave yet! Don't you know what'll happen if those rich fools set their sights on the Burnybaras? Their entire population will be wiped out in no time! I'll pay you whatever you ask, just please help me!

10.Content: You're right... Those poor creatures deserve to live in peace where they belong!

0.Content: Hold it right there! Put the Burnybara down, and no one gets hurt!

1.Content: And just who the heck are you, that old geezer's assistant? Out of my way, punk!

2.Content: You're the one who's in the way!

0.Content: The Burnybara has finally returned to its natural habitat... Thank goodness!

1.Content: It's time for you to go home, too. I already sent word to your granddaughter, she should be coming to get you soon... Hey, there she is! Over here, Nemora!

2.Content: I can't thank you enough for finding my grandfather, Mr. Rowan! Here, this is the payment we each promised you for your help.

0.Content: Excuse me, sir? Do you have any Blue Truffles, by chance?

1.Content: Blue Truffles? Sorry, I just sold out of those... But I have some other ingredients, if you're interested?

2.Content: Sorry, but if you don't have any, then I should get going. Nothing but the best will do for the most lavish feast in town.

3.Content: Sure thing, just let me know if you need anything else!

4.Content: Since I'm going to the Snowy Peaks to do some business, I should pick up a few Blue Truffles while I'm there. I might be able to turn a nice profit if I do!

0.Content: Hello! I'd like to buy some Blue Truffles, please!

1.Content: No problem! A bag will cost you 200 Silver. I've also got some high-quality Dawn Coral Fungi and Pine Mushrooms here, if you need?

2.Content: No thanks, I'm just here for the Blue Truffles today. Would you mind if I paid with a Mithril note?

3.Content: An IOU, huh? You better not be up to something... Well, I guess it's fine, if it's a Mithril note.

0.Content: Here you go! Top-quality Blue Truffles, fresh from the mountain!

1.Content: Those do look pretty good... But I don't need them anymore. Sorry.

2.Content: Huh? Are you sure? You won't find Blue Truffles like this just anywhere, you know! I bet you could cook all kinds of tasty dishes with these!

3.Content: You just came back from the mountains, right? Heh, I suppose they are pretty fresh... But I'm not paying a hair over 500 silver coins for them.

4.Content: 500? But the market price was at least 1,000 silver coins last I checked!

5.Content: You're right, but two days ago, Master Ulmus came to town and showed us how to grow Blue Truffles ourselves! The best part, is that they taste just like the ones that grow in the wild. Only a fool would go picking them in the mountains now!

6.Content: If that's the case, then the market should be flooded with Blue Truffles soon, right?

7.Content: Not just Blue Truffles, but all kinds of mushrooms! Pine Mushrooms, Dawn Coral Fungi, you name it! So how about it, pal? Does 500 silver coins sound like a reasonable offer now?

8.Content: Alright, alright... It's a deal!

0.Content: Greetings, Mayor! I see things are getting very busy. I was hoping to make some investments here next month.

1.Content: Well, then you'll be just in time for the next election for Town Mayor. Perhaps you didn't know? I would hold off.

2.Content: Oh, I'm sure you'll be re-elected! Well, see you later.

3.Content: An election complicates things... I'll check the candidates to shore up my investment.

0.Content: Oh. I just want the election to be over. It's tense enough between the two mining groups. They even fought yesterday.

1.Content: Interesting. So, the two groups of miners support two different candidates separately?

2.Content: Oh yes. That's a really big issue.

0.Content: I support Anasta! Ruby mine workers support Skriath. But if he gets in, he's going to redirect the railways to the rubies. That's as good as dooming our town's economy!

1.Content: There are many workers in ruby mine, right？

2.Content: A lot, sure... But both candidates have got to think about everyone's interests, and reasonable ways of dividing the railway.

0.Content: Hmph! Our family's been hard up these last few years all because Anasta decided to give railway priority to the limestone workers. This time I'm voting for Skriath!

1.Content: Limestone workers used to get priority?

2.Content: Priority? Hah! The limestone mine just has more workers shouting down other voices! Our family works rubies. It's a lot harder with the others using up the railway!

0.Content: I always rest a couple of days after doing the mail. Quite tiring, you know? I can't believe a huge town like this only has one track out.

1.Content: I guess it's hard to make another one—what with the terrain.

2.Content: Yeah. But we've got plenty of valuable minerals here in need of moving. If the post can't catch a ride, they gotta go on foot!

0.Content: Rowan! Are you doing business here too?

1.Content: Heh! Just poking my nose around. Not like you.

2.Content: Well, our foundry needs a new batch of copper ore. My guys just can't get it organized. That's why I'm here.

0.Content: You seem very interested in how the town's doing of late...

1.Content: (Sheepish smile) Heh. Just asking around since I've nothing better to do I guess?

2.Content: What did you ask?

3.Content: Everyone said you're sure to lead the town to greatness!

4.Content: (Who would dare say they support Skriath in your presence?)

5.Content: I certainly hope so. Best of luck with your investments.

0.Content: (Cough) What's with the smoke? Argh! That mountain's on fire! I was hoping to invest in the forest there. What am I supposed to do now?

1.Content: It's my fault... I got careless. And now the whole place is ablaze because of the wind(Cough) First, we need to calm down and organize someone who can control the power of water to put out the fire. Or someone to revitalize the forest.

2.Content: Thank heavens. My business idea is saved! I'll find someone.

3.Content: I'll stay here to put a stop to that wind. Come soon!

0.Content: Greetings! You have mastery over water, right? Could you help put out that forest fire?

1.Content: Very well. I'll put a stop to the raging fire.

0.Content: Greetings! You have mastery over plants, right? Could you help put out that forest fire?

1.Content: Alright. I'll restore the area's vitality.

0.Content: Thank you, all! The place'll be normal again soon.
I've traveled to my fair share of places... And I'm tired.

1.Content: Were you hoping for a thank-you gift? I'm afraid I don't have anything suitable here. But I did notice buried treasure under a pile of leaves when I was trying to put out the fire...

2.Content: Thanks, that'll be fine!

0.Content: Hello, I'd like to purchase some Sage Blueberries. How was the harvest this year?

1.Content: The harvest was fine, but a thief has been making a lot of trouble for us lately. Help us capture that hoodlum, and I'll cut you a good deal on my blueberries!

2.Content: It's a deal!

0.Content: No, please! Have mercy!

1.Content: No can do. You've caused enough problems around here, and that farmer has every right to teach you a lesson.

2.Content: I'm sorry! Please, just let me go, and I swear I'll never steal another fruit for the rest of my life!

3.Content: Ugh... Out! Don't ever show your face!

4.Content: Oh, I can't thank you enough! Here, these are the blueberries I was going to steal. Take them!

5.Content: Huh? Okay...

0.Content: I'm sorry, the thief got away... But not before I managed to knock some sense into him. I don't think he'll be coming back anytime soon.

1.Content: I suppose that works, too. Much obliged, friend.

0.Content: I heard Springs Town has ample sulfur deposits. Perhaps it could make some cash... Huh? Is someone crying?

1.Content: (Sobbing)

2.Content: Ma'am, what happened?

3.Content: My family... in Springs Town... It's been taken over by Hypogeans! Everyone's left!

4.Content: Curses. How can I do business around Hypogean invaders? I promise I'll help you drive them out!

5.Content: Thank you! I'll lead you there!

0.Content: Wonderful! The Hypogeans have fled!

1.Content: Heh! Let me just put my cart somewhere suitable. That'll make my trading a lot easier...

0.Content: Huh. No one's around. It's so... quiet.

1.Content: Maybe they don't know the Hypogeans have been driven out? They're still on the run... Your business will pick up once they come back.

2.Content: Oh, Lira has a relay station nearby. I'll go there to send the word out.

0.Content: Greetings! I have a request to make of you hardworking messengers: if you see anyone from Springs Town, please tell them it's safe to return.

1.Content: Alright. Oh, you're a businessman, right? Please don't park your cart in the middle of the road.

2.Content: Don't worry. My chosen spot won't get in others' way.

0.Content: Hi! I'd like to buy some candy please. Have any jelly candy?

1.Content: Oh, I'm terribly sorry. I don't.

2.Content: My daughter is sick. She'll only take her medicine with really sweet candy. Mind helping me get some from that shop there? Then I'll buy it from you?

3.Content: Hmm. Locals are big fans of this sweet candy, huh? I'll have a look.

0.Content: ... That young mother by the roadside? I know her. Her kid, Astar, isn't doing too well, so she always gets candy for comfort. Pity I just sold out. But the Honey Merchant will be along soon with a new batch of merchandise. Maybe I could trouble you to fetch some of his stock on my behalf? You can find him by the Orchard.

1.Content: OK then. Let's see how the orchard business is going.

2.Content: (Perhaps I can vertically integrate the fruit, honey, and candy industry...)

0.Content: Let me just rub my glasses for a sec while I check the order... OK. Yes. I should send this batch along to the Candy Shop. Here's the honey. Could you pass it along?
Thank you! Wait a second... It's time you also had a try at the most delicious, sweetest jelly candy imaginable! This one is for little Astar. Don't worry about the bill. Least I can do...
Thanks! Now I can finally get Astar to take her medicine. I hope she gets better soon! Thanks so much for your help.
Wow! You have a very impressive foundry!

1.Content: Don't remind me... I just want to make my money back.

2.Content: Aren't foundries always good business? I myself was wanting some helmets and rings.

3.Content: That's it... Rings! Argh. I don't know who started the rumor, but sweethearts today now think it's bad luck to wear the same pair of rings! Now I can hardly sell 'em for a decent price. I've been stressed for a couple of days...

0.Content: Ahoy, young man! That a box of rings in your hands? They wouldn't happen to be Earl-brand?

1.Content: Huh? The rings I just bought here? What?

2.Content: Don't you know? You can't just put on Earl rings—especially not with your girlfriend. It means you'll break up!

3.Content: What?! I was about to propose with these! I'd better get a different set.

4.Content: Don't listen to that tomfoolery! Nothing wrong with Earl rings. He's got some perverse reason to spread that idea! Wait!

0.Content: I admit it! It's a scam.

1.Content: Would you get out of fostering a weird superstition?

2.Content: Oh, I'm just an inventor! I've got a new technique for tastan gold wheel, and I was hoping to go into business with Earl. Problem is, Earl rings are too much of a money-maker for him to ever consider me. And I don't think there are any other workshops up to my level of sophistication. So...

3.Content: So you'll damage his ring business, wait for him to get desperate, and then come back with a new money-maker?

4.Content: Hey! It's not like I have other choices. I'm all in.

5.Content: My fellow merchants are not making us look good.

0.Content: Huh? The general's also paying a visit?

1.Content: The army wants a new batch of helmets. I wanted to talk first. I'll leave the rest to my officers.

2.Content: Bulk buying is good business. I wonder if a smaller merchant such as myself might be able to fill some army orders?

3.Content: I doubt it. But I have been meaning to buy saltpeter from Ore Valley. Do you think I could commission you to transport the gold on your cart there on our behalf?

4.Content: Not sure the transport fee'd be worth much... But I'd be very happy to do business with you! I hope you'll think of me when considering future orders.

0.Content: Halt! Well... what do we have here, my friend? Gold? Here's a deal: let's split it.

1.Content: Friend yourself! Get outta my way!

2.Content: You should be grateful I'd even consider offering half! No respect...

0.Content: Ouch... Curses! It's a robbery! No... I have to make it out of here!
You're late.

1.Content: So sorry. I ran into some thuggery on the way. But I made sure you didn't lose a cent.

2.Content: Excellent. Here's your commission. I'm happy to declare you a reliable merchant. I'm sure we'll see plenty of future opportunities.

0.Content: Hi! I'd like to look at your recent haul. Heard you got a lot of shellfish and salmon?

1.Content: Shellfish perhaps. But hardly any salmon this year. I'm worried something's affecting 'em upstream. Maybe contamination. Mind having a look?

2.Content: Could be a complicated problem...

3.Content: We need to stay in the bay. We have no other choice but to commission you. But I promise if you can help our salmon here, we'll definitely make it worth your while.

4.Content: Alright. Time for some adventuring. I'll let you know if I find clues.

0.Content: Master Sonja! Noticed any nefarious changes along the banks of this waterway recently?

1.Content: What are you asking about? Both sea and wind are fair under my watch here.

2.Content: Thank you. May your ventures prosper!

0.Content: Excuse me? Do you often go here? Seen anything strange in the water recently?

1.Content: No... And I play here almost every day.

2.Content: Apologies. Please keep on!

0.Content: Caught you! You're pouring waste in the river!

1.Content: Lies! You haven't seen anything!

2.Content: You dare deny it?

0.Content: What are we supposed to do? We can't stockpile it or eventually there's gonna be an accident and—kaboom!

1.Content: This isn't true! Last year's salmon was fine. Thanks to you being lazy!

2.Content: We do have a purifier, at the core of which there's a special catalyst thing a mage used to maintain. Unfortunately, Earl and he had fallen out. He left with the catalyst... And now the purifier basically can't do much at all. We just have to dump the stuff.

3.Content: Time to get a new batch of catalysts.

4.Content: There aren't any here. But you might find some in Longleaf Pine. They secrete the precious resin.

5.Content: I might find those around Snowy Peaks, yes? I'll go there. Won't do any good to have untreated explosives in your workshop.

0.Content: ... Now get your purifier up and running! I've got some shellfish I want to buy from the eastern port.

1.Content: The foundry is much safer now! Thanks a lot.

0.Content: So it was dwarves from the foundry? Thanks. I'm sure the salmon will return next year. Then you'll be very welcome to buy as much as you want.

1.Content: Ha! Next year? Let's talk about this year.

2.Content: Very well. Here's a present for you.

0.Content: Eh? Why's there a cannon in the city?

1.Content: It's not a cannon! It's a kind of fireworks stage. Fireworks bring the whole town good luck! The stronger the fireworks, the better our good fortune! You should take a look at the show.

0.Content: I'm getting closer to Harmony City. I should start planning my inventory. This place is going to make me rich!
The Frozen Mother, her voice a clarion call atop the mountaintops, unleashed the first howl of anger, a reminder that Esperia had surrendered to the icy embrace of winter.

1.Content: The land was blanketed in a mantle of snow, a shroud that muffled the sounds and tracks of the animals and beasts.

2.Content: With careful attention, Mishka followed the tracks through the wintery forest, searching for the red figure she had just encountered amidst the snowy wilderness.

3.Content: It was a being that Mishka had never encountered, its red hue standing out against the snowy backdrop. However, the other side seemed hesitant, and Mishka left with only some water and food.

4.Content: With her duties fulfilled, Mishka set out to return to the mysterious creature. As she traced the tracks, her worries intensified. Chancing upon a strange trail, the echoes of a battle reached her ears...

0.Content: Hmph, must be those wretched poachers.

1.Content: But you, little one, you're brave to run around wearing all red. You stand out like a sore thumb in the snow.

2.Content: But don't worry. Just stay behind me and I'll keep you safe.

0.Content: I didn't expect you to be so natural. Your move really caught me off guard.

1.Content: Where are you from, little one? Are you lost? I guess we can travel together...

0.Content: Dammit! Why are there so many poachers on this trip? I'd better tell my teacher about this.

1.Content: Let's go, little one!

0.Content: Good job, fluffy pal!

1.Content: I've gotta hurry and deliver the message. It looks like the poachers are planning something big.

2.Content: Pal, where are you going? If you can't find your way home, why not come to my house?

3.Content: You have to try my grilled fish! It's the best you'll ever taste.
