6.Content: You are surprisingly difficult to destroy, talking artifact. Very well. I shall play your little game.

7.Content: I weave my nest with fine threads, and sting my prey to death. Who am I?

0.Content: Hmm, this might be too easy for you.
An interesting response, but not the right one.
How much longer will I have to put up with the Arachins and these annoying webs? Fine. I shall find another way.
A clumsy attempt to entrap me.
I am a scar of trust, a destruction of promises, a poisonous snake hiding in a garden of flowers, ready to strike the innocent. Who am I?
A close encounter with the Void Fragment may be responsible for the Arachin soldiers' newfound depravity...
What could be more reminiscent of Ankhira than a disgusting, repulsive web?
The foolish Arachins have always believed themselves capable of entrapping anything.

1.Content: But today it is not I but they who will have the worst of their stupid traps.

0.Content: I've had enough of all roadblocks, impediments, and barriers! I consign them to destruction, one and all.

I grow stronger with the passage of time. I am an intangible bond that tightly connects people together. I can create and also destroy empires. People flock towards me and I tempt many to reach for the stars. What am I?
This is where Ankhira used to hide...
Their traps have not been quite as easy as I envisaged.
In all truthfulness, Ankhira has been a continual nuisance for me since day one. Her webs certainly didn't help.
You're nothing if not a persistent obstacle. I ask you: why?

1.Content: You have a great thirst for power, Safiya. Do you not fear that this very same ambition will eventually consume you?

2.Content: Fool! If I were afraid of success, I would not be here but in a jail cell, ready to accept punishments of my usurper.

3.Content: Power corrupts and ultimately enslaves all who desire it. You shall be no exception. You have one hope: abandon the struggle against your former ally. Or else never retreat from the pit of endless desire.

4.Content: Who are you to even speak to me of such things? Ankhira's sympathizer who wants nothing more than for me to let her go?

5.Content: I have no stake in your conflict. I simply exist—and have existed ever since you accepted the lure of the Void. I am not real any more than your rapacious ambition. But just as it exists, so do I.

6.Content: Then who shall I assume I am talking to but a fantasy conjured up by the Void?

7.Content: I'm here to warn you of the point of no return—when you become willing to sacrifice anything and everything for power. Mark my words, it will consume you. It will rob you of the very things you hold of value. But I will still be here—waiting for that moment.

8.Content: Please. As if my ambitions could rob me of what I desire! On the contrary, they empower me! And no one will stand in my way until I've achieved what I so richly deserve.

9.Content: Then I would be delighted to test your resolve.

0.Content: The game of ambition has no end. Not yet. And my former allies? They will be utterly destroyed. In the end only I shall remain.

1.Content: Just you wait, former friends. Wait for the day of my coming, the day of your destruction!

0.Content: Oh Divine Light, what happened to this garden... Judging by these traces of a Magic Circle...

1.Content: Yes, it is a sacrificial Magic Circle for the Hypogeans. Master was right. Earl Barod has forsaken the Divine Light.

2.Content: He will be judged by the Divine Light for his sins.

0.Content: The Hypogeans are still roaming around here. We must comb through the surroundings. There may yet be some survivors.

1.Content: May the Divine Light protect them.

0.Content: We have searched the whole place. Apparently, the Hypogeans have gotten to everyone. We may have defeated the Hypogeans, but...

1.Content: But I'm afraid there are still more Hypogeans craving the souls of the lost.

2.Content: The Temple needs to come up with a solution. The grace of the Divine Light does not reach every corner of this realm. There is still much darkness to be dispelled.

3.Content: I believe the Divine Light will guide us on our quest.

0.Content: What's going on? Where am I? How come I'm some other girl now...

1.Content: Stop messing around, Little Red Riding Hood. Time to go.

2.Content: Go?

3.Content: You're supposed to bring cake and medicine to visit your sick grandmother. Do you remember how to get to her house? Go out of town, through the forest, and she's in the cabin next to the three plum trees.

4.Content: (This is the first page of the storybook! I'm in the book!)

5.Content: (Then I'll just listen to my Mom. This is probably a story about Little Red Riding Hood giving her basket to her grandma. Once the story is over, I should be able to get out of here.)

6.Content: Okay, I'm on my way.

7.Content: Have a safe trip.

0.Content: Oops, I'm Little Red Riding Hood right now and I should stay away from the bear.
Right, I can shake the bluebells to make some noise and make the bear think it's a rabbit or frog, and leave me alone!
BANG——

1.Content: Gunshot? Maybe someone's hunting nearby.

0.Content: Grandma, this is Little Red Riding Hood and I'm here to see you.

1.Content: Hello, child, come give your grandma a hug.

0.Content: Why are your ears so big, Grandma?

1.Content: So I can hear you better.

2.Content: Why is your mouth so big, Grandma?

3.Content: So I can eat you in one bite! Arwoo!

0.Content: What a pretty storybook. Let me check it out... "Once upon a time, there was a cute little girl whose grandma gave her a red riding hood. One day..."

1.Content: Hey, this room...

0.Content: I'm the hunter in the story! Judging by the sun, I'm back to the first page of the book!

1.Content: All right, I'm so strong now, and carry a hunting rifle too!

2.Content: Where did that granny go... I get it, the big bad wolf ate her and changed into her clothes before Little Red Riding Hood got there...

3.Content: I have to hustle to Granny's house and kill the wolf, so Little Red Riding Hood can reunite with her grandma.

0.Content: Ouch, I should lie down for a bit... Wait, no, the wolf is going to eat that granny if I don't make it on time!
Are you in, Grandma? You should hide quickly. There's a wolf on the loose!

1.Content: Humph! You found me. But you're hurt all over and got no chance against me!

0.Content: Geez.

1.Content: Yes, what a feast I'll have for tonight! Arwoo!

0.Content: Rats, I was close to winning! I'm the grandma now and I should run! But no, Little Red Riding Hood is coming...

1.Content: A shame I got hurt before... Hey, if I covered up the trap, the hunter could take the wolf down!

2.Content: But the hunter is hunting right now and won't come to help.

3.Content: If I draw the bear over here, though, the hunter will probably follow! But the bear will eat me too... I got it. I can put bait on the trap!

0.Content: What a nice-smelling plum!
The bear will come for sure!
RARGH—

1.Content: That sounds like a wounded bear... Haha, here's my opportunity!

0.Content: Oh, the bear trap belongs to this old lady...

1.Content: Mr. Hunter, you can have all these bears as long as you'll stay and guard my house for a while. Wolves have been coming around lately.

2.Content: I'm happy to help. Please go hide somewhere.

0.Content: A wolf, I see!

1.Content: There's a hunter here?!

0.Content: Yeah, I'm going to make myself a coat out of wolf skin.
Are you feeling better, Grandma?

1.Content: Much better, Little Red Riding Hood... You're finally here! *sob*

2.Content: Don't cry, Grandma, I'll come see you often from now on!

3.Content: Ever since then, there's no more big bad wolf trying to hurt Little Red Riding Hood and Grandma.

0.Content: Stop dilly-dallying! It's gonna get dark soon!
Stay away from the furnace, girl. It's dangerous!
Your grandmother's eaten my cake. She'll get better soon.
The projected heroes will seal you in the dream permanently. You're not getting out!

1.Content: Preposterous! I am the ruler of the dream realm. The heroes are no match for me.

2.Content: I will defeat you all one by one.

0.Content: You really have the nerve to come back! Guess you're asking to be sealed in again?

1.Content: You know nothing. Dreams are fascinating!

0.Content: If the legends of the Dark Forest are true, I should find the frost-reigning sword master at the very peak of this snow mountain.

1.Content: Without testing this myth, I should hardly consider my training in the sword complete.

0.Content: Portals, I suppose, strange to find them here...

1.Content: Yes, but it's impossible to ascend the mountain by foot from here.

2.Content: I see. And with whom am I speaking?

3.Content: I do not lean on titles, Wilder swordsman. Regard me as a fellow traveler, if you please.

4.Content: By the way, I did see how you fight. There's to admire in your swordsmanship—your mastery of the elements of wind and ice. Perhaps you can use the same to unlock the powers of this Teleport Hub.

5.Content: And what would I have to do?

6.Content: Imbue the Teleport Hub with wind energy, maybe?

0.Content: Right. As you may have guessed, this Teleport Hub can recall or push a portal along a straight line.

1.Content: How is it you know so much about this arcane device and its uses?

2.Content: Conjecture. It's my first experience with these, too. But if I may suggest, mounting the summit may be easier if we work together. What say you to that, swordsman?

3.Content: I'll stand in no one's debt. If I can help you as well, then let it be so.

0.Content: Aha, many of the ruins of our land are filled with these moving relics. Are they a headache to passing adventurers? Yes, but sometimes, they are intriguing as well.

1.Content: I suspect the manipulation of these devices will raise or lower other platforms of the same color. Try it, sir.

2.Content: I must say you are much more knowledgeable than a typical Mauler.

3.Content: Never look down on Maulers, Wilder. I'd say the study of terrains would be among my strong suits.

0.Content: This place... A-choo! Just cold enough to gnaw at my bones.

1.Content: Are you sure you want to press on?

2.Content: Do not worry about me, swordsman. I can handle myself.

0.Content: I can't help but wonder, where is this Snowpeak Swordsman? I've seen nothing of him.

1.Content: Snowpeak Swordsman... You mean that old Wilder ballad?

2.Content: How is it a Mauler knows the legends of the Dark Forest?

3.Content: Ahh... (exhales a warm breath). I suggest we ascend the summit together. There you'll find the answers.

0.Content: Here we are. Ahh (gasping and shivering), this is the peak of my achievement and... test of endurance (shaking) ...the summit!

1.Content: Here's the summit? Then where is the "Snowpeak Swordsman"?

2.Content: Snowpeak Swordsman, an old ballad it is. But if you ask me, I'd say it actually depicts the icy snow and frosty wind on the mountain. In other words, the snow mountain itself wields the blade that reigns frost and wind.

3.Content: Oh, right. I see.

4.Content: You standing here alive with those two swords of yours says a lot about your mastery of the elements already.

5.Content: I could say the same for you, Mauler traveler! What of your scales? Aren't your people more affected by the cold? Why would you risk your life just to come here?

6.Content: I have to better my fear of cold! The Mauler's Enclave has many enemies. Our leader may send me into battle at any moment; I know not where—a marsh, the sea, or even a frigid mountaintop. So I must be ready.

7.Content: I dread to think of what awaits your enemies with that determination. You will be an outstanding scout.

8.Content: And you've also proved yourself a peerless swordsman today. Then can I suggest—before we both freeze to death—that we indulge in a cup of hot soup?

0.Content: Is this... Have we reached the highest peak of this snow mountain?

1.Content: Ye-yee-ss-ss! (shivering) No, this is the second highest peak. I see a taller one on the other side.

2.Content: At least we are on the right track. We'll need to take a turn to follow the ridge.

3.Content: I see. These people weren't so lucky after all (pointing at the frozen corpses by his feet).

4.Content: These warriors scrambled here in search of the Snowpeak Swordsman, but they mistook this for the mountaintop. In the end, they all collapsed here in despair.

0.Content: If there's anything that makes Peggy happy, it's definitely a great forest adventure with Raku!

1.Content: But in a moment of agitation, she left the compass in the room… Now the befuddled duo find themselves lost in the woods amid the thick fog, unable to find a way out after going around in circles. As night falls, Peggy and Raku hold each other tight in fear, frightened by rustling noises in the dark forest.

2.Content: Suddenly, a Shroom Spooder appears in front of them, approaching as if wanting them to follow it. Since they are lost anyway, they decide to just follow the little spider.

0.Content: Raku, is it really okay to follow the spider? You don't suppose it's trying to lure us into its lair and eat us…

1.Content: Well, we can escape now… Oh hang on, the spider has stopped. Peggy, look!

2.Content: Why are all these people holding torches? It's so dangerous! What if they set the trees on fire?

3.Content: I think the spider wants our help.

4.Content: Yes! If the forest is set on fire, we'll all be in danger!

0.Content: Woah! How fast they've fled... Thank god they didn't drop any torch on the ground.

1.Content: Raku, I heard spiders are most afraid of fire. What if these people light up fire again at another location?

2.Content: How awful! Are they trying to burn the forest down?

3.Content: Ah! I remember my uncle saying that some wicked folk catch spiders and sell them for money! These people must be trying to drive the spiders out with fire and then capture them…

4.Content: That's so evil! Let's go after these scoundrels and chase them away!

0.Content: They are gone at last! The spider was amazing. Its black mists sent all those hunters crying and running for their lives!

1.Content: We're reaching the edge of the forest... The little spider has led us out. Finally, we can go home!

2.Content: Yes! Once I'm home, I'll ask my father the King to send troops to protect this forest. We can't let those dreadful hunters hurt the spiders anymore.

3.Content: Alright then, little spider. See you next time!

0.Content: Is this your training range, Morvus?

1.Content: Yes—with enchanted targets that attacked our newest recruits! I first noticed when they dodged our musketfire.

2.Content: Strange. Must have been frightening for them.

3.Content: Targets that can attack you? That means one thing in my book... Hypogeans!

4.Content: A reasonable guess. And there is a distinct Hypogean aura in the air. I fear we face yet another invasion.

5.Content: Our musketfire does nothing! And there's covering on top, too annoying!

6.Content: See the way the Hypogeans organized the targets into a triangle? It's an intelligent attempt at putting on a shield.

7.Content: I'll slay one Hypogean after another if I have to 'til there's an army of them dead. We'll show them this land belongs to us!

8.Content: Morvus, is that cannon still usable?

9.Content: I can't remember if it's still in service, but it should be easy enough to find out.

0.Content: The trusted cannon—the best of dwarven ingenuity at work.

1.Content: Dwarven ingenuity indeed!

2.Content: All we need to do to punch through is just take those Hypogeans out of the triangle formation.

3.Content: This is a perfect moment to blow them to smithereens with the cannons!

4.Content: The barrier's gone! Now we come to target practice. Morvus, would you do the honors?

5.Content: The blasted thing moves in a flash! Is there no end to Hypogean devilry? Watch out!

0.Content: Nice line-up of targets you've got at this shooting range. You train your Marksmen well.

1.Content: Maybe a little too well. I don't want to see another target for a long time.

2.Content: Let's stick to what worked before, and blast that triangle apart. Wait, what's that? A moving platform!

3.Content: Right. Here are the controls if I'm not mistaken.

4.Content: It's our chance! Raise the target so we can break that triangle!

0.Content: We can also change the target's location with this thoughtfully-installed track. We Marksmen love moving targets!

1.Content: Hurry! We should finish the lot of 'em soon!

0.Content: We've finally reached the end of the range and I'm exhausted!

1.Content: Let's save the victory celebration for when we clear the last target.

2.Content: I want to savor the moment, but I can't help thinking our motherland is still in Hypogeans' filthy hands.

3.Content: Take heart, Morvus! We win the war by winning one battle at a time!

4.Content: Trust me, one day we'll fully drive these wretches from our land! And every victory along the way makes us all the stronger.

5.Content: Well said. With the range back in our hands, I'll redouble my efforts to build our cadres into our strongest fighting force yet.

0.Content: Is it me, or does this place seem fancier than before? I almost got lost this time... Ah, the butler is here. Hey, George!
Hey! I'm over here! Let's go. I'm eager to get to the manor.
Ahem... Miss Lotti awaits your presence at the manor. Please head eastward in that direction. I have an urgent matter I need to attend to. I bid you adieu.

1.Content: Wait—

0.Content: Hmph... He hurried off before I could ask questions about Lady Lina's disappearance.
This sign says that the market is to the north and Goldflare Manor is to the east.
May the Divine Light bless Lady Lina and reunite her with Miss Lotti.

1.Content: The notice says whoever finds Lady Lina and brings her back to the manor gets 10,000 gold coins!

2.Content: They must have a great mother-daughter relationship...

0.Content: C'mon, let's go and play in the garden! I've found a secret spot!

1.Content: Lady Lina said we're not allowed in the garden! The last time she caught Tom in there, she sent him home. His father really gave him a talking-to.

2.Content: His father must be really strict with him.

3.Content: That's because his father doesn't want to upset Lady Lina. He works at her factory.

0.Content: Hey you! You're a detective, right? You're dressed like one.

1.Content: Is there something I can help you with?

2.Content: I need a goldflare. I can't seem to find a fresh goldflare around here. I've got a big reward for you if you get one for me.

3.Content: I am a detective, but you should know that Lady Lina never lets anyone touch her goldflares.

4.Content: Yeah, I know. But my little brother's death may be somehow connected to this flower.

5.Content: I found some clues, but the folks in the manor caught me snooping around, and now I'm not allowed near the place. You gotta help me.

6.Content: You'd better give me a big reward for this.

0.Content: Here is a fresh goldflare. I don't see how it's connected to your brother's death, though.

1.Content: That's what I'm gonna find out. Here, take this. This quill is made from the feathers of an Obsidian Finch.

2.Content: This is really rare indeed.

0.Content: Thanks a lot for your help!
Miss Lotti? I almost didn't recognize you. Look how tall you've gotten. You've become an elegant young woman.

1.Content: Thank you for your kind words. Presently, only my mother, myself, and our butler George reside in the manor. Given the circumstances, the responsibility of overseeing our security has fallen upon me.

2.Content: I'm afraid you will need even more security... Can you please tell me in detail about Lady Lina's disappearance?

3.Content: Mother said she was going to the flower garden, and then she never returned. I've looked everywhere but still haven't found her. That is the reason I've asked for you.

0.Content: Don't worry. I will leave no stone unturned. Can you tell me if Lady Lina has been acting differently lately?

1.Content: When you met my mother all those years ago, she was in her prime. But afterward, she became seriously ill and got steadily worse.

2.Content: Recently it's been really bad. She's become absent-minded, and she rambles nonsensically. I can pay you whatever you want. Please, you must find her.

3.Content: My sincerest apologies for what happened... I will start looking around the garden at once.

0.Content: Yes, please find her.

1.Content: My sincerest apologies for what happened... I will start looking around the garden at once.

0.Content: Get outta here! You're scaring the fish away!

1.Content: Once you answer my questions, I'll leave immediately. You seem to have been fishing here for a while. Have you noticed anything unusual lately?

2.Content: You! Hmph... Alright, there was something strange. The manor was built on the edge of the lake, so usually no one can get to the forest.

3.Content: I was out fishing two nights before Lady Lina vanished. Saw a woman in the woods, with her cloak caught on a tree...

4.Content: Umm... what's that guy doing in the tree?

5.Content: I was sober! But couldn't see well, and she just disappeared! You best disappear too, or all my fish'll be gone!

0.Content: So this is a goldflare. Lady Lina wouldn't let me see them last time I was here. People say that these goldflares can heal serious injuries. Mercenaries are buying them up in bulk.
There's no way Lady Lina could've scaled this wall in her current condition... Is there a secret entrance?

1.Content: Hey... There are some broken bits of brick here!

0.Content: Lady Lina didn't just wander off. Someone took her... Then they put the bricks back in place.
Stop right there! You're the one who kidnapped Lady Lina!

1.Content: You don't understand! Lady Lina is evil!

2.Content: You want money, do you not? Let us go, let Lady... Miss Lotti stays in charge of the manor, and she will pay you whatever you want. It won't do her any good if you take us back there.

3.Content: And what good is there for you to do this?

4.Content: I want to save her!

0.Content: Thank you for your mercy. But... I beseech you to beware of Miss Lotti...
Madam, you are saved!

1.Content: You killed him! You bloody killed him!

2.Content: He kidnapped you... You must be confused...

0.Content: George was the one who kidnapped her. I accidentally killed him during the scuffle.

1.Content: Well, thank goodness you were there! Here is your reward, and thank you. I will take Mother up to her room to rest. Until we meet again, I bid you farewell.

0.Content: Mother, why did you try to leave...? You need to rest...

1.Content: Why?! Why did you kill him?!

2.Content: Are you still concerned about George? My initial misgivings regarding his character upon his arrival at the manor have proven to be rather accurate.

0.Content: I'm very sorry. I saw a gap at the side of the garden and found tracks of a rickety cart. Bandits must have taken Lady Lina.

1.Content: I'm worried that the reason you have yet to receive a ransom note is because Lady Lina was too frail. She may already be...

2.Content: Oh, Mother... *sob* *sob* *sob*...

3.Content: Thank you for your trouble. Please accept this token for all your efforts... I need some time alone right now.

0.Content: It was George who took your mother. He wants to try and heal Lady Lina.

1.Content: You let that thieving scoundrel get away? Are you mad? Get out of my sight! I'll rescue my mother myself!

0.Content: Detective Purrrlock, your unexpected presence has placed me in an exceedingly uncomfortable position. This location holds the utmost confidentiality concerning our family's goldflare refinement business.

1.Content: *Chuckle*... Are you sure all this is all business related?

2.Content: Naturally! It is imperative that you pledge to maintain the utmost discretion in this matter. Should our methodology be divulged, everyone would be doing it.

3.Content: Your intentions, I trust, were not deliberate. I shall refrain from pursuing this matter any further. Allow me to accompany you out.

0.Content: This is no common tree... But who would want to disguise a Bloodberry tree as an apple tree and plant it here... and why?
Let me take a look at my notes: Dip a quill in fruit juice, transcribe the teleportation spell, and read out the incantation...
Looks like I still can't cast this spell yet.
Did I get the spell wrong?
Let's take a look at where the teleportation spell has taken me...
Your greed is truly despicable... But I shall not waste my time arguing with you. I must locate my mother.

Detective Purrrlock, your unexpected presence has placed me in an exceedingly uncomfortable position. This location holds the utmost confidentiality concerning our family's goldflare refinement business.

1.Content: *Chuckle*... Are you sure all this is all business related?

2.Content: Naturally! It is imperative that you pledge to maintain the utmost discretion in this matter. Should our methodology be divulged, everyone would be doing it.

3.Content: Your intentions, I trust, were not deliberate. I shall refrain from pursuing this matter any further. Allow me to accompany you out.

0.Content: Hmmm, what should I call you? Lady Lina? Or... Baron Salino? Lady Annette?

1.Content: You've found me out.

2.Content: I also figured out that your goldflares don't heal people. They're parasites that consume life... I will burn your garden down to ensure it doesn't harm another soul!

0.Content: I apologize. I was too rash.

1.Content: Do not worry. You are still my friend.

0.Content: Curses! This vessel was perfect!

1.Content: So this is your true form. Don't worry about getting another vessel. You should've died 200 years ago! I will rectify this mistake!

2.Content: After I destroy you, I will change into another vessel. I shall never perish!

0.Content: Wait! You can't kill me! I'm the Insect Queen!

1.Content: You're about to die, and you're still blabbering on.

2.Content: No! I am what is keeping the parasites restrained. Once I die, they shall all hatch! Then they will kill everyone they've infested until a new Queen is born!

3.Content: Kill everyone...?

0.Content: Don't tell me I have to just let you keep your brood?

1.Content: You should go... before things get any worse. Believe me, this is the best ending you can hope for.

2.Content: No, I will fix this somehow.

0.Content: I won't let you deceive anyone else!

1.Content: Hahaha... You self-righteous fool! You have no idea what disaster you have wrought!

0.Content: Is this some kind of ritual space... It feels really weird here. What is all of this?
The dead tell no tales...

1.Content: Ah—

0.Content: This place once held the historical literature of the Empire. Many scholars have recorded the benevolence of the Divine Light within its pages. The sins of the Hypogeans cannot be forgiven, for destroying it.

1.Content: Even if the Hypogeans turned the pages into dust, traces of the Divine Light will still remain.

2.Content: There are no survivors here, but I still see tracks of the Hypogeans. We must watch out for any ambush.

3.Content: Worry not. The Divine Light will erase all stains of evil.

0.Content: Look at the state of these ruins. I cannot imagine what suffering the scholars must have endured before their deaths.

1.Content: Oh, the benevolent Divine Light, may you protect the souls of the departed.

0.Content: I did not expect to see her here. Betraying the faith and destroying this place––it may be her revenge against the Divine Light.

1.Content: She has corrupted herself and committed the gravest sins. She is no longer one among us. Show her no mercy!

2.Content: Looks like we must annihilate the dark creatures to prevent the tragedy from recurring.

3.Content: The darkness will eventually be dispelled. May the Divine Light grace us with its guidance.

0.Content: Do you really want to go there by yourself, Lyca? It's dangerous! That Hypogean garrison is up in the northern deserts and without the deer's powers... It's all up to you now...

1.Content: If I don't find the Hypogean who has sealed the deer's power, he will attack the Dark Forest the moment that its divine protection is weakened. I have to do this, not just for my deer but also for the forest.

2.Content: Don't worry, Arden. We Dusk Patrollers are never truly alone. Even if I lose my connection with the stars, I still have my companions with me.

3.Content: I see that you have made up your mind, my child... Let nature bless you on your path.

0.Content: Kaz, your skills to conceal yourself are second to none. I need your help to scout ahead and gather intelligence moving forward.

1.Content: Absolutely, Lyca. I am always at your service.

0.Content: Lorsan, you hear words upon the wind. Please find the path forward to the lair of this Hypogean.

1.Content: Of course, sister. Did you think I would sit idly by when you needed my help?

0.Content: The road up ahead is blocked by a spectral disruption... There must be a way to dispel it nearby.

1.Content: Look over!

0.Content: If we activate the device, the spectral disruption should dissipate.

1.Content: Time to speed up.

0.Content: What's going on? I feel a familiar sense of Star Power nearby...

1.Content: I need to find Kaz first. She would know the situation here.

0.Content: Lyca! You finally made it. Guess what I found? There's a sealing stone tablet that's been set by the Hypogean!

1.Content: A sealing stone tablet? Is this what has been sealing the deer's powers...

2.Content: Yes! I have good news as well. I've seen this type of seal before! It normally needs a magic circle to resonate its power. We need to destroy the magic circle to render the seal useless.

3.Content: You must know where the magic circle is, then.

4.Content: Of course. On the right, there are two hidden magic circles that are resonating with the stone tablet.

5.Content: It's just that there are many traps around here. Several Hypogean soldiers are also guarding the magic circle. It's not going to be easy.

6.Content: You have to break the sealed stone tablet first to free the Star Power trapped within. That'll give you a fighting chance when you face the Hypogean.

7.Content: Excellent work. As always, your skills have been invaluable.

8.Content: If we plan accordingly and proceed with caution, we may be able to avoid unnecessary confrontation with the Hypogean foot soldiers.

0.Content: As long the magic circle is destroyed, the seal and tablet connected to it will also be destroyed. The deer's powers will be free once again.

1.Content: But I remember Kaz saying that there was another magic circle hidden here...

0.Content: All the magic circles that were resonating with the stone tablet have been destroyed. The deer's power is returning.

1.Content: Most likely, the Hypogean has already sensed us. We need to be even more vigilant moving forward.

0.Content: As soon as I stepped within these lands, I felt the very essence of the Hypogean in the air... I hope Lorsan has found the lair of our enemy.
Lyca, the rumors all point to the Hypogean lair being on the furthest west side.

1.Content: There are many Hypogean soldiers guarding the path to their lair. We are close, but we will have to fight our way through.

2.Content: Fortunately, I've discovered another secret. You'll find a hidden teleportation gate in the far east region. You can take the portal right to the Hypogean lair.

3.Content: On the far east side... If we take that route, we'll have to deal with all the nasty surprises they left for us...

4.Content: You've got us this far, Lyca. I trust you.

5.Content: Thank you, Lorsan. But I didn't do this on my own. It was you all who helped me along the way.

0.Content: Because of Kaz and Lorsan, this difficult journey was made easier. The power of the Darkness grows every day. This will not be the last threat the forest will face.

1.Content: A time might come when the power of the stars fades from my grasp. Yet, I am certain that my stalwart companions shall stand by my side, and united, we shall conquer the encroaching darkness. Nothing will stand in our way.

0.Content: Whoa! Is this... Pirate Hodgkin's lair?

1.Content: I guess that cannonball blasted both me and Hodgkin away. Why do these things always happen to me...?

2.Content: Damn it! I can't let Hodgkin get away. This is his lair. I bet it's riddled with booby traps. I need to watch my step.

0.Content: Let me guess. Hodgkin drilled this tunnel as an escape route...

1.Content: You're still not dead yet?! My cannons were pointing right at you.

2.Content: It's not been easy to trap the great Immortal into this corner. A cannon ball might have saved your life, but your luck ends here!

3.Content: Hah! You trapped me?! I've drank more than you've had baths, boyo! This is all... um... a part of my plan!

0.Content: You might be mighty out there! But you're on my turf now. Let's see if you can get out alive.

1.Content: I'm taking you with me... even if I have to turn this whole stinking cave upside down!

0.Content: I should've known that little plan wouldn't be enough to stop the Commander of the Thousand Sail Fleet.

1.Content: I'm curious, did this place used to be a tomb before you pirates took it over? There's no other reason for it to be filled with so many traps.

2.Content: And with that big brain of yours, I can't believe you've still not found your treasure.

3.Content: Enough of yer blather! I've been all over this old tomb, and I've found nothin' but traps and tripwires. There ain't no treasure here!

4.Content: I see. There are tripwires here too...

5.Content: You! You're as treacherous as a pirate! Even now, you're tryin' to pump me for information...

6.Content: Even if you do know, so what? You think you can get your hands on it?

0.Content: Incoming!

1.Content: That was close! You reckless fool! Don't rush at me like that!

0.Content: Hahaha! Looks like the Commander of Thousand Sail Fleet is a lot more hot-headed than he seems. Look at the mess you've gotten yourself into now! Why don't you stay here and die?
You can't fool me with your tricks!

1.Content: Ugh! You old eel! Avast!

0.Content: Ha! Fooled you! Now I get to sneak outta here. Don't think you can catch me that easily!
(Muttering) First step here, then step here...

1.Content: Noooo! I went the wrong way!

2.Content: You idiot, I can't believe you tripped a wire and got yourself trapped! Looks like the gods want you brought to justice.

3.Content: There won't be any cannonballs to save you this time. Just surrender.

4.Content: You really think so? I'm gonna blow you to smithereens!

5.Content: Think before you act! Setting off a cannon in this tiny space will collapse the entire tomb on top of us!

0.Content: Stop bluffing! I'm just gonna get rid of this trip wire.

1.Content: Hey, don't go. I didn't get to thank you for opening up the way.

2.Content: Don't get ahead of yourself. You ain't seen nothing yet.

0.Content: The boss was right. There really is some navy scum around here.

1.Content: Hey, minion! Where's your boss?

2.Content: Our boss is retaking the Immortal, and then we're gonna be back like a whirlwind!

3.Content: But just leaving you guys here like this... You know he's basically leaving you here to die, right?

4.Content: Wh-What do you mean?

5.Content: I can deal with a bunch of Graveborns like you in no time, but it'll still slow me down while Hodgkin escapes on the Immortal. Basically, he's left you here for me to grind to dust, you know?

6.Content: Grind to dust?

7.Content: That's our little trick for dealing with Graveborn pirates on my fleet. We throw them into a millstone, and we grind them to dust once and for all so that they can never hurt anyone ever again.

8.Content: You talk a big game for a human! Sailors, let's teach him a lesson!

0.Content: Can't you see all those fleets out there? They're waiting on my orders. Tell me where Hodgkin ran off to and I promise we won't make things difficult for you. I'll pack you up and drop you at Bantus, then you're the army's problem and not mine.

1.Content: Screw Hodgkin! I hate working in this old hunk of junk anyway! He's been using me since I became a Graveborn. Keep your word, and I'll take you to him!

0.Content: (Wipes his sweat) Hahaha! This time I'm gonna get him. This trap is foolproof. Jerome is mine.

1.Content: Looks like you've finally figured out how to set a trip wire. On a scale of one to ten, how'd you do?

2.Content: Shiver me timbers! Where did you come from?! Didn't my Graveborn sailors stop you?

3.Content: People like you don't keep friends for long, Hodgkin. You're fast running out of cannon fodder. You've got nowhere to run.

0.Content: You're the only one out of the entire Lightbearer fleet who has been able to take on the Immortal all these years. But, sooner or later, I'm gonna beat you. Hahahaha!

1.Content: You think you got me trapped? I know exactly what you're thinking. Just be careful you don't screw yourself over.

0.Content: Hahaha! I just opened the deepest part of the tomb and took all the treasure! It won't take long for me to build a new fleet.

1.Content: I wouldn't be so sure about that. Your underlings have already given away all your secrets. I've already earmarked all the treasure to cover the expenses of my fleet. There's nothing left for you!

2.Content: Damn! Surrounded on all sides! Didn't expect a landlubber like you to catch me on the seas! You're in the navy! You're supposed to handle the treasure over to the empire! Not keep it yourself! Who else wants to be a pirate if you do so?!

3.Content: I'll do whatever it takes to rid the world of pirates like you! Now hurry up and get your backside into the dustbin of history where it belongs!

0.Content: Alright, I get it. But rather than letting the navy take me, I'm gonna drag you down to the depths with me, Commander. Watch me blow this tomb and bury us both!

1.Content: Oh no! Hodgkin wants me to die with him! This place is collapsing! Ahhhh!

2.Content: Commander, are you alright? Where are you?

3.Content: I'm here! Hodgkin set off an explosion, and the tomb collapsed. It's dangerous here.

4.Content: You need to retreat for the time being. I have a feeling we need to let him go this time, but Hodgkin has left us a gift. I know he won't be able to live this down. Watch yourself. He'll be back sooner or later.

0.Content: It seems that stepping on all the moving tiles will open the area's barrier.
At a noble manor in Oakenfell, Oscar and Rosaline are making final preparations for a banquet.

1.Content: While preparing the dishes, Rosaline discovers a speaking large radish that broke out of the soil. She informs Oscar of this, and the two come to the backyard to take a look.

2.Content: Just when Oscar is probing into why the "large radish" has appeared, some intruders break the peace at the manor…

0.Content: You truly live up to your name, Rosaline. You sorted out all the dishes for the banquet in a jiffy!

1.Content: It is my duty, Oscar, sir. However…

2.Content: What is it?

3.Content: I saw a large radish that emerged from the soil in the backyard… It's huge and it speaks!

4.Content: A large radish that speaks? How interesting. Let's go take a look.

0.Content: What brazen intruders! Thank god for you Oscar, sir, for noticing them in time.

1.Content: They were making a beeline for this radish… Oh, how rude I am. It's not a radish. Technically speaking, it's a spirit.

2.Content: Oh, my apologies, little spirit, for calling you a radish all this time. Please don't be upset.

3.Content: It seems to have drawn quite a motley crowd of odd characters. I must chase them out first.

0.Content: I've taught these foolish merchants a lesson. They won't be showing up here ever again.

1.Content: Hey little spirit, you must not wander off by yourself again. What if you get eaten as a radish?

2.Content: Haha. It does look delicious indeed. I do not mind adding radish to our menu tonight.

3.Content: Oscar, sir. Please don't make a joke like this. Look how it's burrowed back into the soil… Alright then. You're always welcome back to play at our manor.

0.Content: Robin Hood! You're finally here.

1.Content: My lady, was it you who wrote to me? You seem distressed and in need of rest.

2.Content: Thank you for your concern. Yes, I wrote to you. My daughter is missing. Lord Beckett said you were the only one who could help.

3.Content: Lord Beckett lives in the official lakeside residence on the easternmost side of the manor.

4.Content: Fear not! Of course, I will help. What is your daughter's name, and what was she wearing before she went missing? And her hair—how does she keep it?

5.Content: Um? Th-That... Lord Beckett will be able to tell you. He was the last person to see her.

0.Content: Well, if it isn't the honorable Robin Hood. You probably don't remember, but I wrote to you some time ago asking for help... Alas, you never replied.

1.Content: Tell me, what suddenly brings you to these parts now?

2.Content: Lord Beckett, I've come to make some inquiries. A child has gone missing in your manor. Her mother told me you were the last person to see her.

3.Content: What does she look like, and what was she wearing when she disappeared? Did anyone know her last whereabouts?

4.Content: Yes, a lovely child. Olivia's little Jasmine—didn't Olivia tell you what her daughter looked like? She must be distraught.

5.Content: The girl has golden hair like sunshine on a rainy day. The poor child... There was nothing I could do for her...

6.Content: Well, my good sir. I will help you in your investigation if you will help me. If you can help me retrieve my stolen account book from those bandits north of the manor, I will tell you where Jasmine may be.

7.Content: Account book?

8.Content: Yes, all my business accounts are in that book. One must keep up with one's business, and if it's in the red, how will I be able to support the people of the manor?

9.Content: Brave Robin Hood, you are called the hero of the people. I have faith that you will always do the right thing. Am I not correct?

0.Content: That was a close call. I almost didn't make it, but the bandit leader is dead, and the manor is safe again.
Did you find my account book?

1.Content: Here, take it. Now tell me where Jasmine is, like we agreed.

2.Content: Hahaha, but of course. However, my dear Robin Hood, you don't need to find Jasmine anymore.

3.Content: She was abducted by the bandits, and since you eliminated them, she has returned.

0.Content: I heard that she escaped from the bandits during the chaos. Is she alright? Was she injured?

1.Content: Oh, Robin Hood! I was just looking for you! I want to thank you for saving my daughter...

2.Content: No need. But where is your daughter?

3.Content: Ah... about that... this was a terrible ordeal for her. She's holed up at home and won't come out... Best let her rest a while.

0.Content: Oh! It's a blonde young lady... No, it's a "bandit", I see.

1.Content: You know what I want! That's right! Give me all you've got!

2.Content: Sadly, I don't have any valuables on me. Besides, your mother has been looking for you. She's waiting for you to go home.

3.Content: I don't have a mother. I only have a brother.

4.Content: Oh... It's dangerous out here, little Miss Bandit. If there were any wild beasts about, you'd be done for.

5.Content: You must have snuck out somehow. Let me take you back.

0.Content: Hey! Don't move! This is a robbery! It's been days, but I've finally found a sitting duck like you!
I'm back!

1.Content: Jasmine, where did you run off to? Your brother has been so worried!

0.Content: Where have you been these last few days?! We've been looking all over for you. I was worried that Lord Beckett had you.

1.Content: I wanted to help you hunt in the forest, but I didn't know how! So I decided to rob someone... like you did before!

2.Content: Look who I caught today!

3.Content: Oh no, you really... I'm sorry, sir. Thanks for bringing my sister back.

4.Content: You don't look like you're from around here. You're not from the manor, are you?

5.Content: *Chuckle* Honestly, Lord Beckett did ask me to come here to get his account book back.

6.Content: But I didn't expect that you were Jasmine's brother. So her mother... your mother asked me to find her and bring her home.

7.Content: You've been tricked by that dastardly Lord Beckett. As for that woman, she's just one of the many people in his pocket.

8.Content: Lord Beckett couldn't get anything from us, so he colluded with his minions to kill our parents. He took everything valuable we had. He said it was to repay our debts... I have all the evidence here in his account book.

9.Content: I couldn't let my little sister starve to death, so I became a bandit and brought her here. My other friends here are facing the same thing.

10.Content: My brother's been so good to me! Look at these clothes that he stole for me from that theatre troupe! I could never wear something so nice back home!

11.Content: Hypocritical villains and honorable thieves are as different as night and day... (Rubs his chin) It looks like you lot are not the bad guys in this story.

0.Content: Thank you for your help, sir. We don't have to worry about Lord Beckett exploiting us anymore.

1.Content: From now on, everyone here will live free.
